reviews.text:
Update: Now in video form

There is a house on a hill, and there are people in it. And they're nice, but not really. There is a garden, and there they get a lot of sunlight. And it is nice, and they get to sleep there sometimes.

There is a house underground, and there are people in it. And they're the first to tell you that they're not very nice: they're con-men, grifters, forgers and imposters. They sit among stink bugs, and they've been there for so long that maybe they've convinced themselves that they just belong there.

There is a rock, and it is a gift, but it is also a burden. And maybe it's a metaphor, but it's also just a rock: solid and heavy, difficult to lug around, and dangerous in the wrong hands. Some people will tell you that it's supposed to bring wealth. But again, it's also just a rock.

There is a line, and it cannot be crossed.

There is a smell, and it comes from the underground. And the people who live in the house on the hill can smell it. And the people who live underground try to imagine a life in the sun, a future where they aren't just garbage to be washed away in the rain. But there is a smell that sticks to them, and they know that they can never really belong.

There is a world, and it is nice, but not really. There are houses on hills, and houses underground. There is plenty of sun, but it isn't for everybody. There are people grateful to be slaves, and people unhappy to be served. There are systems that we are born into, and they create these lines that cannot be crossed. And we all dream of something better, but we've been living with these lines for so long that we've convinced ourselves that there really isn't anything to be done.

There is a knife. And it doesn't do much in the long run, but there will always be some satisfaction in crossing some lines.
call me by your name’s cum peach walked so parasite’s killer peach could run
Another Bong hit.
Our expectations were high but HOLY FUCK
a question to people who rate this 4.5: what more do you want literally what more do you want
Woh, that kid is going to need a much bigger trauma recovery cake.
The tent won’t leak. It’s from America.
morse code me by your name and i'll morse code you by mine

One detail I noticed this time around is that Min and Mr. Park both react the same way to being asked if they like or love the people that they're romantically involved with– by laughing. And in Mr. Park's case, giving a sarcastic answer that undercuts his saying 'yes'. Min and Mr. Park are both seen as powerful figures deserving of respect, and the way they dismissively respond to an earnest question about whether they truly care for the people they're supposed to tells us a lot about how powerful people think about not just the people below them, but everyone in their lives.

"I just feel comfortable here. It feels like I was born here. Maybe I had my wedding here, too. In my old age, love will comfort me."

A murder.

The most thrilling scene in years.

post.description:
Delivery fee quote for a Canadian street address (POST /api/v1/store/{n}/can-deliver, the order app's delivery eligibility check): the delivery fee, service fee rate, small order fee and its threshold, minimum order and estimated delivery time. Without `location_number` the delivering store is resolved first (POST /api/v1/search/find-delivery-store). No cart, order or payment is created. An address the site will not deliver to returns `fee_status: not_deliverable` with null fees.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

location_number.description: Optional store number (locationNumber from search_stores). When omitted, the store the order app would assign to this address is used. Unknown store -> not_found.

state.description: Two-letter province or territory code (ON, QC, BC, ...). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2}$.

street.description: Street address line, e.g. 1010 Gerrard St E. Delivery fees are quoted per address.

zip.description: Canadian postal code, with or without the space (M4M 1Z3). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z][0-9][A-Za-z] ?[0-9][A-Za-z][0-9]$.

post.description:
Menu listing for a store from `search_stores`. Prices and the item set differ per store; there is no national menu. Follow with `get_menu_item` (by `item_code`) or `get_custom_pizza_options`.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

category.description: Optional category filter: the item type code (e.g. `LRP`), the category name, or its slug (e.g. `large-14-round-pizzas`); case-insensitive. Unknown category -> not_found.

language.description: Language: `en` (en-CA) or `fr` (fr-CA): French names and descriptions, same prices.

location_number.description: Little Caesars store number (`locationNumber`), as returned by `search_stores` and used in the public store page URL https://littlecaesars.ca/en-ca/store/{n}/.

service_method.description: Service method: `pickup` is the BFF's serviceMethod 1 (In-Store), `delivery` is 4 (Deliver Now).

post.description:
Details for an `item_code` from `get_menu`. The Canadian site has no per-item modifier endpoint: flavour or drink choices are separate items, and create-your-own toppings come from `get_custom_pizza_options`.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

item_code.description: Item code from `get_menu` (e.g. `HNR-CA14PEP`), case-insensitive; it is also the last segment of an order-app item URL.

language.description: Language: `en` (en-CA) or `fr` (fr-CA): French names and descriptions, same prices.

location_number.description: Little Caesars store number (`locationNumber`), as returned by `search_stores` and used in the public store page URL https://littlecaesars.ca/en-ca/store/{n}/.

service_method.description: Service method: `pickup` is the BFF's serviceMethod 1 (In-Store), `delivery` is 4 (Deliver Now).

response.description: Large round pizza with Pepperoni.
response.name: Classic Pepperoni

default.description: Error response; upstream passthrough responses may use provider formats

post.description:
Build-your-own pricing and the complete topping catalogue for a store. Pass `crust_id` to keep the answer small; the whole menu is about 100 KB upstream.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

crust_id.description: Optional crust/item id (e.g. 102000 Custom Round); unknown id -> not_found.

language.description: Menu language: `en` sends cultureCode en-US, `es` sends es-US (Spanish names and descriptions, same prices).

location_number.description: Little Caesars store number (`locationNumber`), as returned by `search_stores` and used in the public store page URL.

service_method.description: Service method the menu is priced for: `pickup` is the BFF's serviceMethod 1 (In-Store), `delivery` is 4 (Deliver Now).

default.description: Error response; upstream passthrough responses may use provider formats

x-aisa-response-pending.reason: public success response has no authoritative payload declaration

post.description:
Deals and promo codes; combine with `dma_code` from `search_stores`/`get_store` or pass `zip`. Not store-scoped menu prices: use `get_menu` for those.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

dma.description: Market (DMA) code such as `MID` (Detroit) or `DCW`; case-insensitive. Returns national deals plus those targeting this market. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9]{2,6}$.

language.description: Menu language: `en` sends cultureCode en-US, `es` sends es-US (Spanish names and descriptions, same prices).

zip.description: US ZIP code; resolved to the closest store's DMA code (GET closest-dma-store). Mutually exclusive with `dma`. Pattern: ^[0-9]{5}$.

post.description:
Delivery fee quote for a US street address (POST /api/v1/store/{n}/can-deliver, the order app's delivery eligibility check): the delivery fee, service fee rate, small order fee and its threshold, minimum order and estimated delivery time. Without `location_number` the delivering store is resolved first (POST /api/v1/search/find-delivery-store). No cart, order or payment is created. An address the site will not deliver to returns `fee_status: not_deliverable` with null fees.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

location_number.description: Optional store number (locationNumber from search_stores). When omitted, the store the order app would assign to this address is used. Unknown store -> not_found.

state.description: Two-letter US state or territory code. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2}$.

street.description: Street address line, e.g. 2211 Woodward Ave. Delivery fees are quoted per address.

zip.description: US ZIP code (5 digits). Pattern: ^[0-9]{5}$.

post.description:
Menu listing for a store from `search_stores`. Prices and the item set differ per store and per service method; there is no national menu. Follow with `get_menu_item` for modifiers and toppings.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

category.description: Optional category filter: a displayGroupId (e.g. `84`), the category name, or its slug (e.g. `large-round-pizzas`); case-insensitive. Unknown category -> not_found.

language.description: Menu language: `en` sends cultureCode en-US, `es` sends es-US (Spanish names and descriptions, same prices).

location_number.description: Little Caesars store number (`locationNumber`), as returned by `search_stores` and used in the public store page URL.

service_method.description: Service method the menu is priced for: `pickup` is the BFF's serviceMethod 1 (In-Store), `delivery` is 4 (Deliver Now).

post.description:
Modifiers for an `item_id` from `get_menu` (items with `has_customizations` true carry options or toppings).

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

language.description: Menu language: `en` sends cultureCode en-US, `es` sends es-US (Spanish names and descriptions, same prices).

location_number.description: Little Caesars store number (`locationNumber`), as returned by `search_stores` and used in the public store page URL.

service_method.description: Service method the menu is priced for: `pickup` is the BFF's serviceMethod 1 (In-Store), `delivery` is 4 (Deliver Now).

response.description: Large round pizza with Pepperoni
response.name: Classic Pepperoni

upgrades.description: Large Detroit-Style Deep Dish Pizza with Pepperoni
upgrades.name: Detroit-Style Deep Dish Pepperoni

upgrades.description: Large thin crust pizza topped right to the edge with Pepperoni and Cheese.

upgrades.description: Large round pizza with more Pepperoni and Cheese than our Classic pizza.
upgrades.name: ExtraMostBestest® Pepperoni

upgrades.description: Large round pizza with more Pepperoni and Cheese than our Classic pizza, plus a ring of cheese baked into the crust.
upgrades.name: Stuffed Crust Pepperoni

post.description:

post.description:
For the Hot Deals / Value Menu / Catering Bundles categories, which menu lists without items. Defaults to the public, currently valid coupons.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

category.description: Category id or name to restrict to (e.g. 13 or Hot Deals).

include_expired.description: Also return coupons outside their start/end window.

include_hidden.description: Also return coupons the source marks hidden (loyalty, channel-specific, code-only).

include_items.description: Attach item_groups: every item and size each coupon applies to (large for brand-wide offers).

language.description: Culture of the names and descriptions returned; the source ships both in every file.

store_key.description: Six-character Marco's store key, e.g. LPPPLA (from stores: store_key; also the id= parameter of order.marcos.com/?id=KEY). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9]{6}$.

post.description:
After menu, with an item_id from it, when the caller needs toppings and customization prices for one product.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

language.description: Culture of the names and descriptions returned; the source ships both in every file.

store_key.description: Six-character Marco's store key, e.g. LPPPLA (from stores: store_key; also the id= parameter of order.marcos.com/?id=KEY). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9]{6}$.

response.description: Our hand-made dough baked with our three fresh signature cheeses and garlic sauce, served with a side of our original pizza sauce and ranch
response.name: CheezyBread

default.description: Error response; upstream passthrough responses may use provider formats

post.description:
After stores. Omit category for the whole menu (about 100 items), or pass a category id or name for a slice. Deal categories hold coupons, not items: read them with deals.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

category.description: Category id (e.g. 1) or name (e.g. Pizza, case-insensitive) to restrict items to.

language.description: Culture of the names and descriptions returned; the source ships both in every file.

store_key.description: Six-character Marco's store key, e.g. LPPPLA (from stores: store_key; also the id= parameter of order.marcos.com/?id=KEY). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9]{6}$.

items.description: Ham, salami, provolone cheese, banana peppers, sliced Roma tomatoes, red onions and sub dressing

city.description: City name to filter on (case-insensitive, exact match on the store's city).

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page's next_cursor.

latitude.description: Query point latitude; requires longitude. Results are sorted by distance.

radius_miles.description: Only with latitude/longitude: keep stores within this distance (default 25).

state.description: Two-letter US state code to filter on (case-insensitive). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2}$.

zip.description: Five-digit ZIP; matches the store's own ZIP or a ZIP in its delivery area. Pattern: ^[0-9]{5}$.

Van Rijswijk Tweewielers, Al 109 jaar de fietsenmaker van Tilburg.

Sinds 2015 mag Van Rijswijk Tweewielers zich bij Koninklijke Beschikking Hofleverancier noemen wegens het lange bestaan.

Dé plaats voor nieuwe fietsen, elektrische fietsen, occasions, reparatie en deskundig advies.

Wij dealer van de volgende merken:

Fietsen, elektrische fietsen en bakfietsen:

- Trek
- Advanced Ebike Das Original
- Cortina
- Urban Arrow
- Van Raam aangepaste fietsen

Verder heeft Van Rijswijk Tweewielers een breed assortiment accessoires en onderdelen op voorraad voor fietsen, bromfietsen, oldtimers en scooters.

In onze ruim uitgeruste werkplaats repareren wij alle merken fietsen, elektrische fietsen en bakfietsen.

Als uw tweewieler schade heeft kunnen wij hiervan een schade expertise maken wat geaccepteerd wordt door alle verzekerings maatschapijen.

Als uw tweewieler defect is en u kunt hem zelf niet na onze werkplaats brengen voor reparatie hebben wij ook een ophaal service, Neem hiervoor contact op met ons om een afspraak te maken.

U kunt bij ons ook een verzekering afsluiten voor uw tweewieler, Wij zijn een volmachtbedrijf van ANWB, Enra en Kingpolis verzekeringen.

Heeft u nog vragen neem dan contact met ons op of kom langs in onze winkel. De koffie staat altijd klaar !

post.description:
Finding second-hand or new items for sale in the Netherlands: call with a query, then narrow with category_id/subcategory_id from categories, filters from filters, min_price/max_price, postcode/distance_km, condition or sort. Take listing_id into listing for the full description, bids and seller profile.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

category_id.description: Top-level category id from a previous result's categories (an entry with parent_id null), e.g. 445 Fietsen en Brommers.

condition.description: Item condition (Nieuw, Zo goed als nieuw, Gebruikt, Refurbished, Niet werkend); several values match any of them. Same as filters {"condition": [...]}.

distance_km.description: Only listings within this many km of postcode; needs postcode.

filters.description: Chosen filters as key/value pairs: keys are a returned filter's key, values one of its values[].value (or an array of them for multi_select filters). Example: {"delivery": "Verzenden", "offeredSince": "Een week", "storage": ["128 GB", "256 GB"]}. A key or value the search does not offer is rejected as invalid_input.

page.description: Result page, 30 listings per page; pass next_page from the previous result. The site serves at most max_page pages.

postcode.description: Dutch postcode, e.g. '1012 AB'. Results then carry their distance from it. Pattern: ^[1-9][0-9]{3} ?[A-Za-z]{2}$.

query.description: Search keywords as typed in the Marktplaats search box, e.g. 'fiets' or 'iphone 15'. Optional when category_id is given.

sort.description: Result order from the site's sort menu: relevance (default), newest or oldest listing date, price low to high, price high to low.

subcategory_id.description: Subcategory id from categories (an entry whose parent_id is category_id); needs category_id.

post.description:
Listing payments into or out of an address, finding when it first or last moved funds, or paging through its full history. Use `get_transaction` for one transaction's full inputs and outputs.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->

<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

address.description: Bitcoin mainnet address: base58 P2PKH (`1...`) or P2SH (`3...`), bech32 segwit v0 (`bc1q...`) or bech32m taproot (`bc1p...`); or a `https://mempool.space/address/<address>` URL. Checksums are verified; testnet addresses are rejected. Pattern: ^(?:[13][1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{25,34}|[bB][cC]1[02-9ac-hj-np-zAC-HJ-NP-Z]{8,87}|https?://(?:www\.)?mempool\.space/\S*)$.

after_txid.description: Return the confirmed transactions older than this one; pass the previous page's `next_after_txid`. Pattern: ^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$.

post.description:
Seeing which coins an address can still spend, their sizes and ages. Use `get_address` for just the balance (it works for addresses of any size).

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->

address.description: Bitcoin mainnet address: base58 P2PKH (`1...`) or P2SH (`3...`), bech32 segwit v0 (`bc1q...`) or bech32m taproot (`bc1p...`); or a `https://mempool.space/address/<address>` URL. Checksums are verified; testnet addresses are rejected. Pattern: ^(?:[13][1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{25,34}|[bB][cC]1[02-9ac-hj-np-zAC-HJ-NP-Z]{8,87}|https?://(?:www\.)?mempool\.space/\S*)$.

post.description:
Listing what a block contains or finding its coinbase transaction. Use `get_transaction` for a row's full inputs and outputs.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

hash.description: Block hash (64 hex characters) or a `https://mempool.space/block/<hash or height>` URL. Send `hash` or `height`, not both. Pattern: ^(?:[0-9a-fA-F]{64}|https?://(?:www\.)?mempool\.space/\S*)$.

height.description: Block height (0 = genesis). Send `hash` or `height`, not both.

start_index.description: Position of the first transaction (multiple of 25, default 0); pass the previous page's `next_start_index`.

default.description: Error response; upstream passthrough responses may use provider formats

post.description:
Discovery: find products by keyword or browse a category (e.g. "Graphics Cards|518") for a given store_id. Use lookup_by_sku for a known SKU and get_product for full details.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

category.description: Category facet as the site writes it in fq=category:{Name}|{id}, e.g. "Graphics Cards|518" or "Computer Parts|94".

in_store_only.description: true (default): only items in stock at store_id (myStore=true). false: include out-of-stock and not-carried items.

page.description: 1-based page; default 1. Use next_page from the previous call.

query.description: Keyword search (Ntt). Optional when category is given.

sort.description: Sort order; default match.

store_id.description: 3-digit zero-padded store number (045 St. Louis Park, 205 Phoenix, 141 Columbus). Default 029 = Shippable Items (web pricing, no store inventory). list_stores returns the ids. Pattern: ^[0-9]{3}$.

response.content:
Despite millions of years of evolution, the development of the human fetus remains a complex process that is vulnerable to genetic, environmental, and metabolic disruptions. These disruptions could result in developmental abnormalities, starting with one of the first organs to begin developing in the fetus that continues to develop after birth: the brain.

In a routine prenatal ultrasound, the sonographer will flag possible brain abnormalities for additional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). But imperfect imaging can result in missed or incorrect diagnoses.

To assist with the early detection and treatment of these abnormalities, researchers at MIT, Boston Children’s Hospital, and Inria have developed and trained a deep learning model called E(3)-Pose that helps image the fetus’s head while it’s in motion to capture a high-resolution image that the radiologist can examine. A paper about the work was presented at the [2026 European Conference on Computer Vision](https://eccv.ecva.net/).

“One of the problems with having the baby move is that the slices are all over the place,” says first author Ramya Muthukrishnan. Muthukrishnan is an MIT PhD student in the lab of Sunlin (1966) and Priscilla Chou Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science Polina Golland, who is a principal investigator at the [MIT Abdul Latif Jameel Clinic for Machine Learning in Health](https://jclinic.mit.edu/) (Jameel Clinic) and the MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL).

By slices, Muthukrishnan is referring to a series of 2D images taken during a fetal MRI scan. These 2D planes stacked together effectively make up one high-resolution, 3D image of the fetus’s head. But if the head shifts during imaging, each 2D image “slice” could end up being taken from a different angle, resulting in gaps in the final scan and unusual slice orientation. These problems may cause the physician reviewing the MRI to miss or incorrectly diagnose a pathology in the fetal brain.

“There are very fine details that you need a very good volumetric picture of the brain to see,” explains Muthukrishnan. “If you have coverage gaps, you can’t see critical regions, and you need to be able to see well to detect abnormal development.”

What makes E(3)-Pose particularly good at tracking fetal motion is its focus on physics. Rather than simply training the model to learn physics from the data, the very principles of physics are baked into the neural network: left-right symmetry of the fetal head is embedded in the model architecture, making it easier for the model to accurately identify the brain’s orientation.

When Muthukrishnan began working on the project at the start of her PhD, she had no background in physics, let alone MRI physics. Most of her experience was in computer science. “I was surprised when I had to go and implement this on the scanner,” she recalls. “I was not prepared for how many times I would crash the scanner because putting things on hardware and getting it to work on hardware is a different beast than training a model to run on data on a GPU.”

Despite the challenges, Muthukrishnan persisted. She remembers shadowing a radiologist who performed fetal MRI scans at Boston Children’s Hospital at the start of her PhD and observing the shared frustration of the patient and radiologist: the pregnant mother felt uncomfortable after spending an hour in an MRI, only to quit the scan halfway; the radiologist was unable to procure a full, high-quality MRI to monitor the development of the fetus.

“Seeing frustration about it helped me decide what I wanted to do with my PhD, because it felt like this was a pain point,” Muthukrishnan says.

Fortunately, she had help: Co-author Borjan Gagoski, an assistant professor of radiology at Harvard Medical School and a researcher at Boston Children's Hospital, developed a sequence that acquires additional MRI scans to assist with training E(3)-Pose and worked with Muthukrishnan to help troubleshoot the scanner whenever it crashed. Co-author and Boston Children’s Research Assistant Aryn Lee recruited the pregnant volunteers and assisted with acquiring each of the MRI scans. Senior authors who helped guide the project include Elfar Adalsteinsson, MIT professor of electrical engineering and computer science; Ellen Grant, the Käthe Beutler Professor of Pediatrics and professor of radiology at Harvard Medical School; and Golland. Benjamin Billot, a researcher at Inria and a former postdoc in Golland’s group, helped Muthukrishnan get started with the initial method he developed.

“Ramya’s work elegantly combines geometric concepts like equivariance and symmetry with the power of deep learning to change how MRI scanners acquire the images, and to ultimately help the physicians detect and treat problems early in development. It’s an impressive research project that is deep and fundamental in how it models image acquisition, with clear clinical impact,” says Golland.

Grant, who directs the Fetal Neonatal Neuroimaging and Developmental Science Center (FNNDSC) at Boston Children’s, adds that Muthukrishnan’s work “will automate fetal brain MRI, replacing today's slow, manual process with faster and more comfortable scans for mothers, while also providing higher-quality images for radiologists to interpret.”

E(3)-Pose’s applications could extend beyond motion tracking for fetal MRIs. It could assist with imaging other hard-to-image anatomy, and even autonomous driving applications, where limited sensors need to capture noisy, 3D data in order to track 3D objects.

For now, Muthukrishnan hopes to improve E(3)-Pose so that it can help with imaging second-trimester or younger fetuses, as the model is primarily trained on third trimester fetuses. Second-trimester fetuses are “so small, they move around a lot more because there’s more space in the uterus,” Muthukrishnan says. “They’re more important to focus on because the earlier you detect brain abnormalities, the easier it is to intervene.”

This work is supported by the MIT Jameel Clinic, the MIT Takeda Program, the Chou Family Transformative Research Fund, the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, and the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development.

response.content:
What tasks should artificial intelligence be trusted with, and when should humans remain involved? Designing those decision rights is one of the defining challenges companies face in the AI era.

Researchers from the [MIT Center for Information Systems Research](https://cisr.mit.edu/) have [created a framework that can help](https://cisr.mit.edu/publication/2026_0601_AIDecisionMatrix_SebastianWeillHaskampVomBrocke). Using the AI Decision Matrix, business leaders can determine how humans and autonomous AI agents should participate in decision-making based on two dimensions: ambiguity and risk.

[Ina Sebastian](https://mitsloan.mit.edu/faculty/directory/ina-maria-sebastian), [Peter Weill](https://mitsloan.mit.edu/faculty/directory/peter-weill), [Thomas Haskamp](https://www.wi.uni-muenster.de/department/bpm/people/thomas-haskamp), and [Jan vom Brocke](https://janvombrocke.com/) developed the matrix after conducting interviews with 30 executives. It’s based on the premise that not all decisions are equal: Some are predictable and low risk, while others are ambiguous and consequential.

“This requires different approaches to automation and oversight,” the researchers write in a recent research briefing. “The same AI capability can be safe in one context and risky in another.”

## Dimensions and steps involved in decision-making

The AI Decision Matrix considers two dimensions of decision-making:

- **Ambiguity**, which describes how clearly data determines the answer and to what extent people agree on it. Low-ambiguity decisions are repeatable and predictable, while high-ambiguity decisions allow for multiple interpretations.
- **Risk** refers to the consequences of getting a decision wrong. Low-risk decisions have little impact if they’re wrong and can be easily reversed. High-risk decisions can have significant financial, operational, or reputational impacts if they’re wrong. They are also harder to course-correct.

Making a decision also involves three components:

**Framing**, which defines the problem, assumptions, stakeholders, constraints, and criteria for success.

**Acting**, which is the process of gathering information, evaluating proposed options, recommending and authorizing actions, and executing approved steps.

**Learning**, which is when outcomes are monitored and analyzed, there’s accountability for outcomes, and the decision system is updated over time.

## Fine-tuning human and AI interactions

Considering both high and low levels of ambiguity and risk results in a matrix of four decision types.” Each decision type suggests a different role for AI in the three components of decision-making. Companies should assign decision-making activities to humans and AI accordingly while maintaining human oversight across all of them.

The researchers used One New Zealand, a telecommunications provider with more than 50 AI agents in operation as of early 2026, to illustrate how decision rights can be designed.

**Routine decisions (low ambiguity, low risk).** Routine decisions are well defined and will have limited negative consequences if the wrong choice is made, which makes them strong candidates for automation. Companies can codify framing in advance and automate the action and learning aspects of the decision process. Humans should remain closely involved while confidence in agent performance builds.

**Example:** One New Zealand developed a process for creating audience segments for targeted marketing campaigns. An AI agent translates marketer requests into SQL queries, reducing time spent on segmentation by 60%. The marketing team then reviews the AI-generated segmentation plan before launch, and the AI is granted more autonomy as confidence builds in its abilities.

**Consequential decisions (low ambiguity, high risk).** These are well-defined decisions where potential errors can have significant negative consequences. Here, it’s important to balance automation and human intervention. Humans should continue to monitor execution, manage exceptions, and focus on continuous learning.

**Example:** One New Zealand is using AI agents in customer service to facilitate plan upgrades and to support ticket resolution. Business leaders established the company’s risk tolerance to guide what’s acceptable for automation. For example, inaccurate pricing information was deemed a nonnegotiable constraint, so all decisions related to pricing require a human in the loop. Because the company focuses on continuous learning, agents are introduced gradually, and outcomes are validated before agents are released at scale.

**Exploratory decisions (high ambiguity, low risk).** This class of decisions involves interpretation, creativity, or uncertainty, but errors will have limited consequences. Framing can evolve through human and AI interaction, with humans overseeing actions and continuous learning. Governance must be a priority as experimentation leads to higher-risk use cases.

**Example:** One New Zealand’s marketing team employs agents for content creation tasks, maintaining humans in the loop to help frame goals and learn from customer responses. The team is now using what they have learned to develop agent-led, end-to-end autonomous marketing campaigns. The benefits: AI expands the team’s options and accelerates experimentation while human workers remain on hand to revise mistakes before they can have a major impact.

**Strategic decisions (high ambiguity, high risk).** These decisions involve both uncertainty and significant potential consequences, which means that they require a great deal of human leadership and oversight. People need to take the lead in the framing and learning processes while AI facilitates action.

**Example:** One New Zealand uses automation to optimize its network and improve resilience in the event of power outages. Fifteen task-based agents analyze network data. A set of orchestration agents manages those task-based agents while also providing data and analysis to support human decision-making. Actual decisions remain human-led because they involve trade-offs between service reliability, customer experience, cost, and infrastructure priorities.

## Best practices for designing decision rights

Several steps that One New Zealand has taken to facilitate decision rights design offer guidance for other companies. Among them:

**Make organizational adjustments.** One New Zealand empowered business units with responsibility for framing each AI use case to ensure that agents are anchored in business need, value, and domain expertise. This also ensures that decision rights are developed and applied consistently.

**Create an AI center of excellence.** The company’s center of excellence for AI and data has ownership of data foundations, architecture, and delivery. As part of its work, the center has established a unified data platform for structured and unstructured data; a horizontal AI orchestration layer to coordinate across agentic platforms; a responsible AI use policy; and an iterative rollout to support aligned decision-making.

**Ensure continuous agent management.** Ongoing agent management is crucial to reducing risk. At One New Zealand, deployed AI agents must have a named human agent owner to ensure accountability for outcomes and learning. Human owners are responsible for monitoring performance, refining data, testing accuracy, and improving agents over time.

**Manage AI as a portfolio of business decisions.** As AI is embedded in core processes, leaders need to look beyond individual use cases and consider the business decision that the AI implementation affects. Decision rights for routine and consequential decisions can deliver near-term efficiency gains and help with scale, while exploratory and strategic decisions can unlock longer-term value through innovation and better judgment.

“Companies that get this right will move faster, reduce risk and build trust in how they use AI,” the authors write. “The important shift is from asking where AI can be used to manage the business decisions it shapes.”

[Read the research: “Designing Decision Rights for AI”](https://cisr.mit.edu/publication/2026_0601_AIDecisionMatrix_SebastianWeillHaskampVomBrocke)

---

[***Ina Sebastian***](https://mitsloan.mit.edu/faculty/directory/ina-maria-sebastian) *is a research scientist at the* [*MIT Center for Information Systems Research*](https://cisr.mit.edu/)*. Her work focuses on how organizations create value from AI and other digital technologies, including AI-enabled business models, AI decision rights and trust, new organizational designs, and digital ecosystems.*

[***Peter Weill***](https://mitsloan.mit.edu/faculty/directory/peter-weill) *is a senior research scientist at the MIT Sloan School of Management and chairman of MIT CISR. His work explores future trends, such as digital business models, IT investment portfolios, and AI maturity models, to help organizations maintain a competitive edge.*

[***Thomas Haskamp***](https://www.wi.uni-muenster.de/department/bpm/people/thomas-haskamp) *is an academic research fellow at MIT CISR and an assistant professor in the department of information systems at the University of Münster.*

[***Jan vom Brocke***](https://janvombrocke.com/) *is an academic research fellow at MIT CISR, a professor and chair of information systems and business process management at the University of Münster, and director of the European Research Center for Information Systems.*
key_points: Modern enterprises face the daunting challenge of determining what tasks artificial intelligence can safely perform without human oversight.
The AI Decision Matrix can help business leaders assess ambiguity and risk when granting decision rights to humans and AI.

Routine decisions, which have low ambiguity and low risk, are strong candidates for automation, whereas strategic decisions, which have high ambiguity and high risk, need a strong human lead. Human oversight remains important across all categories of decisions.
response.summary: The AI Decision Matrix uses ambiguity and risk to determine the optimal decision-making structure between humans and AI automation.
response.title: A framework for determining when AI can make decisions

Find archive records (magazines, photographs, reports, adverts, catalogues) by keyword, or list everything of one file format or reference number; take the returned `id` to get_record or, for folders, to list_folder.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。

collection_id.description: Restrict to one top-level collection: a term of the `xip.top_level_so` facet (a uuid, with or without the SO_ prefix), e.g. 82e5314d-48d7-4fb9-bbf4-cf0878a6fc35 for Staff Magazines.

folder_id.description: Scope the search to one folder's hierarchy: an SO_<uuid> structural object id (from list_folder or a result item of kind folder), or a pasted folder page URL.

format.description: Restrict to one preservation file format: a term of the `xip.format_group_r_Preservation` facet, e.g. pdf, jpeg, mpeg-video.

page.description: 1-based result page (50 hits per page). A page past the last one answers not_found.

query.description: Keyword(s), as typed into the site's search box. May be empty when a filter (collection_id, format, reference_number or folder_id) is given.

reference_number.description: Archival reference number (Refno) filter, e.g. CR/D/3/2 or HO/3/2/2/2. The site matches loosely (parent and sibling references can appear); compare `metadata` Reference Number from get_record when exactness matters.

sort.description: Result order: the site's relevance ranking, or title ascending / descending.

board.description: DBPR board code as used by the site's Board select (e.g. 06 Construction Industry Licensing Board, 25 Real Estate Commission). Name searches only. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,3}$.

city.description: City of the main address, as the site spells it (e.g. TAMPA). Name searches only.

county.description: Florida county code as used by the site's County select (e.g. 39 Hillsborough, 47 Leon, 23 Dade; 79 Out of State, 80 Foreign). Name searches only. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,2}$.

cursor.description: Continuation from a previous page: `<page>:<total_records>` as returned in `continuation`. Send the same search fields again. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,6}:[0-9]{1,9}$.

exact_prefix.description: The site's 'Search Names Beginning with Exactly What You Typed' checkbox (SearchPartName=True). In the recorded samples it did not change the result set.

include_historic.description: SearchHistoric=Y: also return licenses that are no longer current.

last_name.description: Individual's last name (the site matches from the beginning of the name).

license_number.description: Exact license number as printed by the DBPR (e.g. CFC056678, SL3295874, CAM9515). When given, the name fields and filters are ignored except include_historic and per_page.

license_type.description: The site's LicenseType code within the board (e.g. 0604 with board 06). Name searches only; requires board. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,6}$.

org_name.description: Organization / establishment name or name fragment (e.g. AARDVARK).

per_page.description: Rows per page (the site's RecordsPerPage choices).

state.description: Two-letter state of the main address (e.g. FL). Name searches only. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2}$.

post.description:
Start here with any Workday career-site URL. Read `facets` to filter by location, job category, time type or remote type (parameters differ per employer), page with next_offset, then call get_job with a result's external_path or url for the full description.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

career_site.description: Any URL of a Workday career site: https://{tenant}.wd{N}.myworkdayjobs.com/{site} (an /en-US/-style locale segment, a search-results URL with ?q= and facet parameters, or a posting URL are fine) or https://wd{N}.myworkdaysite.com/recruiting/{tenant}/{site}.

facets.description: Filters as Workday exposes them: each {parameter, ids} uses a facet parameter and value ids from a previous search_jobs `facets`. Values within one parameter are ORed, parameters are ANDed. When omitted, facet parameters in a pasted search-results URL apply.

limit.description: Results per page; Workday serves at most 20.

offset.description: Result offset: 0 for the first page, then the previous page's next_offset. Workday serves only the first 2000 results of a query.

query.description: Keyword search over the site's postings (Workday searchText). Omit to list everything. When omitted, a pasted URL's ?q= applies.

response.attribution: Source: the named employer's Workday career site

response.body_text:
Key Points

It's been 10 years since Berkshire Hathaway first invested in Apple stock.

It has been the company's largest holding since 2017.

The Apple position encompasses many of Buffett's investing tenets.

10 stocks we like better than Apple ›(function(){ var m=document.getElementById("pit-c897e6a6-2dcd-4f50-aa4f-aee0c6c63ef8"); if(!m||!window.IntersectionObserver)return; var c=m;while(c&&!c.dataset.pitchPlacement)c=c.parentElement; if(!c)return; var fired=false; new IntersectionObserver(function(es,obs){ if(fired||!es[0].isIntersecting)return; fired=true;obs.disconnect(); new Image().src="https://api.fool.com/infotron/infotrack/seen/?impression=c897e6a6-2dcd-4f50-aa4f-aee0c6c63ef8&pitch_id=17995&placement=keypoints_pitch_feed_partner"; },{threshold:0.5}).observe(c); })();

Of all the great investments that former Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRKA) (NYSE: BRKB) CEO Warren Buffett made over the years, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) might have been his best.

Up until his first investment in Apple in 2016, or perhaps with a position he opened in International Business Machines (NYSE: IBM) in 2011, Buffett had been reluctant to invest in technology stocks because he said he didn't fully understand them.

Missed AI’s "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we’re only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

But he soon understood Apple enough to make it his largest holding and best investment. Over the years, Berkshire has made more than $100 billion on Apple stock, Buffett told CNBC back in July of this year.

Former Berkshire Hathaway CEO Warren Buffett. Image source: The Motley Fool.

Best business in the world

Back in 2020 on CNBC, Buffett called Apple "probably the best business I know in the world," adding that he doesn't think of Apple as a stock. "I think of it as our third business." That would be a third business along with insurance and railroads.

That first investment in Apple stock was 9.8 million shares in the first quarter of 2016, when the stock traded at about $25 per share. It was just the beginning of Berkshire Hathaway's commitment to Apple, which Buffett himself discussed at the 2026 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder meeting back in May.

"About 10 years ago, we made a commitment to essentially move 10% of the total resources of Berkshire Hathaway. We turned it over to another person who was not that well known at the time, and we did that by spending roughly $35 billion buying stock in Apple Corp," Buffett said. "I would like to report that 10 years later, several things have happened. One is that the $35 billion -- counting dividends, realized appreciation, and unrealized appreciation -- has turned into $185 billion pretax."

Apple became Berkshire's largest holding by the end of 2017, representing about 15% of the total portfolio. Six years later, by the end of 2023, Berkshire had amassed a $174 billion investment in Apple, which made up a staggering 50% of its $347 billion portfolio.

After that, Buffett began paring back Berkshire Hathaway's Apple position. Part of it was surely profit-taking, but he also said in a recent interview that he was wary about having one stock take up 50% of the portfolio. Apple is still Berkshire's largest position, but it's "only" a $66 billion investment, making up 22% of the total portfolio.

The perfect Buffett investment

There are key takeaways from Berkshire's long-term commitment to Apple that illuminate some of Buffett's investing tenets. One is to buy great businesses at fair prices. In early 2016, Apple stock had slumped and was trading at a deep discount, at just 10 times earnings, its lowest valuation in 10 years.

It also represents Buffett's belief in investing in companies with strong leadership and management -- in this case, former Apple CEO Tim Cook. "When we made our investment and turned over 10% of Berkshire's resources, we were turning it over to Tim. As I say, he has turned that into $185 billion pretax," Buffett said at the shareholder meeting. "I think it's appropriate if Tim Cook would take a bow and our shareholders would say thanks to him."

Further, Apple had, and has, the kind of industry leadership and competitive moat that sets it up for long-term success. And of course, the 10-plus year investment in Apple shows the value of holding on to a great investment for the long term, even though Buffett himself recently admitted that he might have sold too soon on Apple.

But overall, Berkshire's investment in Apple isn't just a great example of the benefits of long-term investing. It also represents, perhaps, the perfect Buffett investment -- the culmination of everything he looks for in a stock.

Should you buy stock in Apple right now?

Before you buy stock in Apple, consider this:

The Motley Fool Stock Advisor analyst team just identified what they believe are the 10 best stocks for investors to buy now… and Apple wasn’t one of them. The 10 stocks that made the cut could produce monster returns in the coming years.

Consider when Netflix made this list on December 17, 2004... if you invested $1,000 at the time of our recommendation, you’d have $387,158!* Or when Nvidia made this list on April 15, 2005... if you invested $1,000 at the time of our recommendation, you’d have $1,365,749!*

Now, it’s worth noting Stock Advisor’s total average return is 932% — a market-crushing outperformance compared to 211% for the S&P 500. Don't miss the latest top 10 list, available with Stock Advisor, and join an investing community built by individual investors for individual investors.

See the 10 stocks »

*Stock Advisor returns as of September 21, 2026.

Dave Kovaleski has no position in any of the stocks mentioned. The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Apple, Berkshire Hathaway, and International Business Machines. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy.

post.description:
Fetch one storm event with its track points and fatality records when the EVENT_ID and the data year are known.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->

event_id.description: EVENT_ID as in the CSVs and the event page URL.

year.description: The data year whose files hold the event (BEGIN year).

event.episode_narrative: A front moving through brought a squall line through western Massachusetts and into central Massachusetts producing pockets of damaging winds which downed several trees.
event.event_narrative: In Princeton, there were downed trees and wires near Ball Hill Rd.

Full collection of a year's details, locations or fatalities rows. Pass type and year for the first page, then only the cursor.

cursor.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page; carries the segment, so type and year may be omitted (if given they must match).

year.description: Data year (the `d` part of the file name), 1950 to the current year.

post.description:
Start here to find a NEVO code by food name or to list the foods of a group; pass the code to get_food for the full nutrient table or several codes to compare_foods.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

continuation.description: Cursor from a previous page's meta.page.next_cursor.

food_group.description: Exact food group name in the requested language, as returned by list_food_groups (for example 'Kaas' in nl, 'Cheese' in en). Case-insensitive.

lang.description: Label language for food group names and nutrient labels; the data is the same in both.

nutrients.description: Nutrient column tags to return per food instead of the default energy and macronutrient set, for example ['SUGAR_g', 'NA_mg', 'VITC_mg']; see list_nutrients. Matching is case-insensitive and 'ug' may stand for 'µg'.

query.description: Free text matched case-insensitively against the Dutch name, the English name, the synonym and the NEVO code; every whitespace-separated word must match. Omit it to list a whole food group.

response.attribution: NEVO-online versie 2025/9.0, RIVM, Bilthoven

Every written customer review for a Newegg US item, 100 per page: rating, title, text, pros, cons, public display name, ISO submission time, purchased-from-Newegg flag, helpful votes and photo count, plus the item's review total and star distribution. Sort newest, helpful, highest_rating or lowest_rating; page with next_cursor until it is null. For incremental sync use sort newest and stop at the first known review_id, or pass since.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

cursor.description: Opaque `next_cursor` from the previous page. Omit for the first page and keep `sort` unchanged while paging.

item_number.description: Newegg item number as used by product: N82E16819113793, 19-113-793 or marketplace 9SIC3DRM4F6818. Marketplace listings return the review pool shared by their product group. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{3,23})[A-Za-z0-9]$.

since.description: Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD). With sort newest, returns only reviews submitted on or after it and stops paging at the first older review. Reviews carry a stable review_id for de-duplicating the overlap. Pattern: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$.

sort.description: Review order. Use newest for incremental sync: submitted_at is non-increasing across pages.

post.description:
To verify a New Jersey license number: status, dates, status change reason and whether a public board action is on file.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

facility.description: Which register to search; omit to try person then business.

license_number.description: The full license number as the site prints it, e.g. 26NO09001800 (nursing), D07351800 (CDS), 25MZ00081700 (acupuncture). Case-insensitive.

response.board_action_note:
Please visit DCA's website to see the final disposition documents.
* A "YES" in the "Board Action" field indicates that the licensee has a public record of some form of action on file with the Board/Committee. Board actions may come in the form of a Consent Order, Cease and Desist Order, Interim Order, Reprimand, a finalized Uniform Penalty Letter, agreed upon Settlement Letter or Final Order. In some instances, "Yes" will represent that a public record of a pending matter such as an Administrative Complaint or a Provisional Order of Discipline may have been filed with the Board/Committee. Such documents represent the filing of allegations by the Attorney General, and do not represent a finding of misconduct until the matter is adjudicated by the Board. Contact the Board/Committee directly to obtain a copy of such documents.
response.discipline_info: For discipline information prior to January 01, 2010 please contact the Board of Nursing via bondiscipline@dca.njoag.gov.

default.description: Error response; upstream passthrough responses may use provider formats

respondent_narratives.name: INTERACTIVE BROKERS CORP
respondent_narratives.text:
Release Number 8794-23
CFTC Orders Interactive Brokers to Pay $20 Million for Recordkeeping and Supervision Failures for Widespread Use of Unapproved Communication Methods
September 29, 2023

Washington, D.C. — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an order simultaneously filing and settling charges against Interactive Brokers Corp., an introducing broker, and Interactive Brokers LLC, a futures commission merchant, for failing to maintain and preserve records that were required to be kept under CFTC recordkeeping requirements, and failing to diligently supervise matters related to their businesses as CFTC registrants.

The order requires Interactive Brokers to pay a $20 million civil monetary penalty, to cease and desist from further violations of recordkeeping and supervision requirements, and to engage in specified remedial undertakings. Interactive Brokers admits the facts detailed in the order.

Case Background

The order finds from at least 2019 to the present, Interactive Brokers failed to stop its employees, including those at senior levels, from communicating using unapproved communication methods, including messages sent via personal text and WhatsApp. The firm was required to keep certain of these written communications because they related to the firm’s CFTC-registered businesses. These written communications generally were not maintained and preserved by Interactive Brokers, and the firm generally would not have been able to provide them promptly to the CFTC if and when requested. 

The order also finds the widespread use of unapproved communication methods violated Interactive Brokers’ internal policies and procedures, which generally prohibited business-related communication taking place via unapproved methods. Further, some of the same supervisory personnel responsible for ensuring compliance with the firm’s policies and procedures themselves used non-approved methods of communication to engage in business-related communications, in violation of firm policy.

Since December 2021, the CFTC has imposed $1.117 billion in civil monetary penalties on 20 financial institutions for their use of unapproved methods of communication, in violation of CFTC recordkeeping and supervision requirements. [See CFTC Press Release Nos. 8470-21; 8599-22; 8699-23; 8701-23; 8762-23; 8763-23]

Related Civil Actions

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) today also announced entry of an order filing and settling charges against Interactive Brokers and imposing a civil monetary penalty for recordkeeping and supervision violations related to the use of unapproved methods of communication.

******

The CFTC Division of Enforcement staff responsible for this action are Devin Cain; Alejandra de Urioste; R. Stephen Painter, Jr.; Lenel Hickson, Jr.; and Manal M. Sultan.

-CFTC-

post.description:
The user wants the official practice participation or injury designations for a week (e.g. '2026 Week 3 injury report', 'Falcons practice report'). Defaults to the current league week.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

season.description: Season year (e.g. 2026). Defaults to the current league calendar season.

season_type.description: Season type: PRE, REG or POST (case-insensitive). Defaults to the current calendar phase, REG for other seasons. Pattern: ^([Pp][Rr][Ee]|[Rr][Ee][Gg]|[Pp][Oo][Ss][Tt])$.

team.description: Club UUID (e.g. 10400200-f401-4e53-5175-0974e4f16cf7) or NFL abbreviation (ATL, AZ, KC, LAR, LV, WAS...). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$.

week.description: Week number. Defaults to the current league week (required when `season` is not the current season).

default.description: Error response; upstream passthrough responses may use provider formats

x-aisa-response-pending.reason: public success response has no authoritative payload declaration

advisory.description: Advisory number (12, 012) or intermediate public advisory (12A). Omit for the latest. Pattern: ^\s*[0-9]{1,3}[A-Za-z]?\s*$.

storm_id.description: ATCF storm id: basin al (Atlantic), ep (eastern Pacific) or cp (central Pacific), the two-digit cyclone number and the season, e.g. al092024 (Hurricane Helene). Case-insensitive. Find ids with active_storms or season_storms. Pattern: ^\s*([Aa][Ll]|[Ee][Pp]|[Cc][Pp])[0-9]{6}\s*$.

sections.heading: WATCHES AND WARNINGS
sections.text:
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:

The government of the Cayman Islands has issued a Tropical Storm
Warning for Grand Cayman.

SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:

A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* Cabo Catoche to Tulum, Mexico
* Cuban province of Pinar del Rio

A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* Grand Cayman
* Rio Lagartos to Tulum, Mexico
* Cuban provinces of Artemisa, and Pinar del Rio, and the Isle of
Youth

A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Dry Tortugas
* Lower Keys south of the Seven Mile Bridge

A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, in this case within
the next 24 to 36 hours.

A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area.  A watch is typically issued 48 hours
before the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force
winds, conditions that make outside preparations difficult or
dangerous.

A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.

Interests along the northeastern Gulf Coast, including the Florida
Panhandle and the Florida west coast, should monitor the progress of
this system.  Additional watches or warnings will likely be
required tonight and Tuesday.

For storm information specific to your area in the United
States, including possible inland watches and warnings, please
monitor products issued by your local National Weather Service
forecast office. For storm information specific to your area
outside of the United States, please monitor products issued by
your national meteorological service.

sections.heading: DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
sections.text:
At 800 PM EDT (0000 UTC), the disturbance was centered near latitude
18.3 North, longitude 82.3 West. The system is moving toward the
north-northwest near 7 mph (11 km/h).  A northwestward motion is
expected on Tuesday and Tuesday night, followed by a faster
northward to north-northeastward motion on Wednesday and Thursday.
On the forecast track, the center of the system is forecast to move
across the northwestern Caribbean Sea through Tuesday night, and
then over the eastern Gulf of Mexico on Wednesday and Thursday.

Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Strengthening is expected during the next few days, and the system
is forecast to become a hurricane on Wednesday and continue
strengthening on Thursday as it moves across the eastern Gulf of
Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high ...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).

sections.heading: HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
sections.text:
Key Messages for Potential Tropical Cyclone Nine can be found in
the Tropical Cyclone Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDAT4 and
WMO header WTNT44 KNHC and on the web at
hurricanes.gov/text/MIATCDAT4.shtml

RAINFALL: Potential Tropical Cyclone Nine is expected to produce
total rain accumulations of 4 to 8 inches over western Cuba and the
Cayman Islands with isolated totals around 12 inches. Over the
eastern Yucatan Peninsula, 2 to 4 inches of rain is expected with
isolated totals over 6 inches.  This rainfall brings a risk of
considerable flooding.

Over the Southeastern U.S., Potential Tropical Cyclone Nine is
expected to produce total rain accumulations of 3 to 6 inches with
isolated totals around 10 inches, bringing a risk of flooding, some
of which could be considerable.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with
Potential Tropical Cyclone Nine, please see the National Weather
Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic, available at
hurricanes.gov/graphics_at4.shtml?rainqpf and the Flash Flood Risk
graphic at hurricanes.gov/graphics_at4.shtml?ero

STORM SURGE: The combination of a dangerous storm surge and the
tide will cause normally dry areas near the coast to be flooded by
rising waters moving inland from the shoreline.  The water could
reach the following heights above ground somewhere in the indicated
areas if the peak surge occurs at the time of high tide...

Dry Tortugas...1-3 ft
Florida Keys...1-3 ft

Storm surge could raise water levels by as much as 2 to 4 feet above
normal tide levels in areas of onshore winds along the southern
coast of Pinar del Rio, Cuba, including the Isle of Youth.

Storm surge could raise water levels by as much as 2 to 4 feet above
ground level in areas of onshore winds within the warning area along
the east coast of the Yucatan Peninsula.

WIND: Hurricane conditions are possible within the watch areas in
Cuba and Mexico by early Wednesday. Tropical storm conditions are
expected in the warning areas in Cuba and Mexico beginning on
Tuesday.  Tropical storm conditions are possible in the watch area
beginning on Wednesday.

SURF: Swells generated by the system will affect the southern coast
of Cuba and the Yucatan Peninsula of Mexico during the next couple
of days.  Swells will spread northward toward the west coast of
Florida and the northeastern Gulf Coast on Wednesday and Thursday.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather
office.

The government of the Cayman Islands has issued a Tropical Storm

SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:

A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...

* Cuban province of Pinar del Rio

A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* Grand Cayman
* Rio Lagartos to Tulum, Mexico
* Cuban provinces of Artemisa, and Pinar del Rio, and the Isle of
Youth

A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Dry Tortugas

A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, in this case within
the next 24 to 36 hours.

A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area.  A watch is typically issued 48 hours
before the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force
winds, conditions that make outside preparations difficult or
dangerous.

A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.

Interests along the northeastern Gulf Coast, including the Florida
Panhandle and the Florida west coast, should monitor the progress of
this system.  Additional watches or warnings will likely be
required tonight and Tuesday.

For storm information specific to your area in the United
States, including possible inland watches and warnings, please
monitor products issued by your local National Weather Service
forecast office. For storm information specific to your area
outside of the United States, please monitor products issued by
your national meteorological service.

----------------------
At 800 PM EDT (0000 UTC), the disturbance was centered near latitude
18.3 North, longitude 82.3 West. The system is moving toward the
north-northwest near 7 mph (11 km/h).  A northwestward motion is
expected on Tuesday and Tuesday night, followed by a faster
northward to north-northeastward motion on Wednesday and Thursday.
On the forecast track, the center of the system is forecast to move
across the northwestern Caribbean Sea through Tuesday night, and
then over the eastern Gulf of Mexico on Wednesday and Thursday.

Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Strengthening is expected during the next few days, and the system
is forecast to become a hurricane on Wednesday and continue
strengthening on Thursday as it moves across the eastern Gulf of
Mexico.

* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

current conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather

post.description:
Crash-test ratings for a year/make/model, or for the ncap_id returned by search_vehicles or decode_vin.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

make.description: Make as NHTSA lists it (case-insensitive), e.g. 'toyota'.

model.description: Model as NHTSA lists it (case-insensitive), e.g. 'camry'.

default.description: Error response; upstream passthrough responses may use provider formats

x-aisa-response-pending.reason: public success response has no authoritative payload declaration

x-codeSamples.label: Reference example

  --url https://api.aisa.one/apis/v1/firecrawl-alexandria/nhtsa-gov/recalls/safety_ratings \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "alexandria": {
    "provider": "nhtsa-gov",
    "capability": "recalls/safety_ratings",
    "options": {
      "request": {
        "make": "toyota",
        "model": "camry",
        "model_year": 2020
      },
      "response": {
        "count": 2,
        "make": "TOYOTA",
        "model": "CAMRY",
        "model_year": 2020,
        "observed_at_ms": 1790225026130,
        "vehicles": [

              "complaints": 7,
              "investigations": 0,
              "recalls": 0
            },
            "description": "2020 Toyota CAMRY 4 DR AWD",
            "dynamic_tip_result": "No Tip",
            "electronic_stability_control": "Standard",
            "forward_collision_warning": "Standard",
            "front_crash_driver_side_rating": "5",

complaints.summary: My car sputters and dies while driving. It looses power when I push the gas to take my turn at a light or intersection. The emergency brake has come on multiple times with no one in front of me.  These have all occurred multiple times since mid 2021
The transmission is premature wearing due to excessive heat causing pump to overheat

2020 Toyota Camry XSE, VIN [XXX], 2.5L 4-cylinder A25A-FKS engine, built at Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky (TMMK) during the production window covered by NHTSA Recall 20V-064 (Toyota campaign 20TA04), which addresses porosity in engine castings that can cause internal and external coolant leaks, engine overheating, and possible engine failure. Toyota’s VIN lookup returns this vehicle as not affected by the campaign, but the failure pattern matches the recall defect exactly. Timeline of failures and repair attempts: XXX, at approximately 92,832 miles, Camelback Toyota in Phoenix, AZ (RO XXX). Check engine light active. Diagnosed DTC P268115 (Engine Coolant Bypass Valve Circuit, Short to Battery or Open). Battery also failed load test. Overheating symptom noted on the same repair order. Coolant bypass valve replacement recommended. Following that visit, water pump and thermostat were replaced at Berge Toyota (Mesa/Gilbert, AZ area). Camelback Toyota stated the vehicle was fixed. Vehicle overheated again the next day after being returned as repaired. XXX, at 93,034 miles, Camelback Toyota (RO XXX). Oil and filter change performed under good faith goodwill service, transmission fluid exchange completed. Overheating condition persisted. Vehicle continued to overheat through the summer and into September 2026. Current dealer now recommends head gasket replacement and states that if the head gasket does not resolve the overheating, the engine block is cracked and the engine will need replacement. Dealer describes the engine as “sucking air,” indicating combustion gases entering the cooling system and/or a compromised block-to-head seal. This failure sequence — persistent overheating, multiple failed repair attempts across two Toyota dealers, replacement of water pump, thermostat, and coolant bypass valve without resolution, and dealer conclusion pointing to a cracked engine block — matches the failure mode described in NHTSA Rec INFORMATION REDACTED PURSUANT TO THE FREEDOM OF INFORMATION ACT (FOIA), 5 U.S.C. 552(B)(6)

entries.markdown: Two new Notion MCP tools move content to Trash after the user confirms. `notion-delete-pages` moves up to 20 pages, and `notion-delete-databases` moves up to 20 databases with their rows. Both need the update content capability. Locked pages and databases can't be moved to Trash. To undo a deletion, use `notion-restore-pages` or restore the item from Trash in Notion. See [Supported tools](/guides/mcp/mcp-supported-tools.md).
entries.title: Delete pages and databases in Notion MCP

entries.markdown: Four new Notion MCP tools change existing comments. `notion-update-comment` replaces the text of a comment the user wrote, and `notion-delete-comment` deletes one. `notion-set-discussion-resolved` resolves or reopens a discussion. `notion-set-comment-reaction` adds or removes the user's emoji reaction. The tools need a Business or Enterprise plan. Get comment and discussion IDs from `notion-get-comments` or `notion-create-comment`. See [Supported tools](/guides/mcp/mcp-supported-tools.md).
entries.title: Edit, delete, and react to comments in Notion MCP

response.content:
Notion’s ethos has always been technology meets the liberal arts. To build the best tools for thought, we refuse to treat engineering and design as separate jobs. This shapes what we build and who we hire.

And almost no one represents that ethos better than Max Schoening.

When Max joined Notion last year, he [described](https://www.notion.com/blog/software-should-bend-welcome-max-schoening) himself as a *Tüftler*, someone who tinkers until something works. This year, he and the team shipped two of our biggest launches: Custom Agents for everyday knowledge workers and our Developer Platform, which lets people and agents extend Notion to fit how they work.

And now, Max is stepping into the role of CTO. While Max has been our product and design leader for the last year, he’s an engineer by trade and has built as much as he has designed. He ran design early on at Heroku (the original PaaS) and worked on Cloud Run at Google. At GitHub, he spent six and a half years working on GitHub Issues, Pull Requests, GitHub Actions, and cloud development environments—tools that millions of developers use to build and ship software.

Max has spent his career making complex infrastructure feel simple, mostly for developers. At Notion, he’s doing the same for founders, builders, and businesses of all kinds.

He believes in open platforms that put customers first. So do we. Openness and agent-neutral context benefit all of our customers, from a small coffee business wrestling with its wholesal
response.description: The org chart of the future will be multidisciplinary, and we’re lucky to have Max lead our technical organization into this future.

response.content:
## Rate limits

The Notion API enforces two rate limits: a per-connection limit and a per-workspace limit. Some endpoints also have their own limit.

### Per-connection limit

Each connection has a fixed budget of requests per 60-second window, based on the workspace's plan:

| Workspace plan | Limit |
| :- | :- |
| Business and Enterprise | 600 requests per minute (an average of 10 per second) |
| All other plans | 180 requests per minute (an average of 3 per second) |

The budget can be spent at any pace within the window — spread out evenly or in a single burst. When a request exceeds this limit, the `Retry-After` value is the time until the window resets, so it is at most 60 seconds.

[Querying a data source](/reference/query-a-data-source.md) has a separate limit of about 3 requests per second per connection. A request over this limit returns an HTTP 429 response with a `Retry-After` header. The [JavaScript SDK waits](https://github.com/makenotion/notion-sdk-js#automatic-retries) for `Retry-After` and retries for you. If you call the REST API directly, see [Retry rate-limited requests](#retry-rate-limited-requests).

### Per-workspace limit

A separate limit is shared across all of the workspace's connections and scaled to the workspace's plan. Because it's shared, requests can be rate limited even when each individual connection is within its per-connection limit. `Retry-After` for this limit can be longer than a minute.

releases.notes:
# Hermes Agent v0.22.4

**Release Date:** October 21, 2026

Patch release. Desktop stops showing suggestion pills above the composer, plus small plugin and dashboard fixes, for the CLI and installer, the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud.

## Fixes

- **Desktop no longer shows suggestion pills above the composer.** The pills appeared for no clear reason, mostly nudging you to set up MCP servers. They and the helpers that only they used are gone. (#142559)

- **Plugins that install nothing skip the dependency consent step.** A plugin that declares no dependencies, or whose `pyproject.toml` installs nothing, now enables without an empty consent prompt. (#142569)

- **Dashboard: WhatsApp can be safely re-paired after logging out.** (#142439)

- **Desktop plugin review:** the surface lint no longer flags prototype writes; reviewers check them by hand. (#142586)

- **Desktop: the approval-mode chip follows the active profile's mode.** (#142565)

response.content:
## How It Works

Two files make up the agent's memory:

| File | Purpose | Char Limit |
|------|---------|------------|
| **MEMORY.md** | Agent's personal notes — environment facts, conventions, things learned | 2,200 chars (~800 tokens) |
| **USER.md** | User profile — your preferences, communication style, expectations | 1,375 chars (~500 tokens) |

Both are stored in `~/.hermes/memories/` and are injected into the system prompt as a frozen snapshot at session start. The agent manages its own memory via the `memory` tool — it can add, patch, or remove entries.

:::caution One agent per Hermes home
Don't point two agent processes at the same Hermes home directory. Memory writes are automatic and load back into the system prompt at session start, so two writers sharing one home will compound each other's entries into state neither of them (nor you) authored. Memory is scoped per [profile](../profiles.md) by design — give a second agent its own profile, and if they need shared memory, use an [external memory provider](./memory-providers.md) instead.
:::

:::info
Character limits keep memory focused. Memory does **not** auto-compact: when a
write would exceed the limit, the `memory` tool returns an error instead of
silently dropping entries. The agent then makes room itself — consolidating or
removing entries in the same turn before retrying (see [What Happens When Memory
is Full](#what-happens-when-memory-is-full)). Note that `patch` is also bound
by the limit: a patch that lengthens an entry can still overflow, so the new
text must be shortened (or another entry removed) to fit.
:::
response.description: How Hermes Agent remembers across sessions — MEMORY.md, USER.md, and session search

response.desktop_packages:
Download the package for your platform from the
[Hermes website](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/).

- **Windows:** open the `.appinstaller` download with Windows App Installer.
  It installs the signed MSIX bundle and records its update source.
  Microsoft Store packages have separate Store ownership.
- **macOS:** open the DMG, then copy `Hermes.app` to Applications. The ZIP
  artifact carries the signed app used by the automatic updater.

Bundled packages contain the agent, Python, supported dependencies, and prebuilt
interfaces. First launch does not build that base runtime. Provider access and
optional integrations can still require network access.

A `Hermes-Setup` bootstrap installer is different: it downloads a source
installation and builds the desktop app. See [Hermes Desktop](../user-guide/desktop.md).

There is no separate remote-only Desktop download. To use Desktop with a Hermes
backend on another machine, install one of the packages above and connect it
from **Settings → Gateways**; see
[Connecting to a remote backend](../user-guide/desktop.md#connecting-to-a-remote-backend).

:::note
The macOS installer is **Apple Silicon only**. macOS on x86 (Intel) processors is [not a supported platform](./platform-support.md#unsupported).
:::
