post.description:
Read what audiences wrote about a book, film or show on Google Play, page by page.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

continuation.description: Token returned by the previous page.

country.description: Storefront country (`gl`), ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Default US. Selects currency and availability. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2}$.

item_id.description: Play id of the title (volume id for ebooks, audiobook id, movie id, show id). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{6,40}(\.P)?$.

item_type.description: Kind of title the id names; must match the id. Google Play attaches TV reviews to the show only: a season or episode id is refused (invalid_input) with a pointer to the show id, which `show` returns.

language.description: UI language (`hl`), e.g. en_US, en, fr. Default en_US. Selects the language of titles, descriptions and labels. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2}([_-][A-Za-z]{2,4})?$.

sort.description: `most_relevant` (default) or `newest`. Rating sort is not supported by the store RPC.

reviews.text: Getting through this book was like walking through sand the way the Fremen walk through sand, which is somehow slower than the way normal people walk through sand. I think the concepts are interesting, like props to Herbert for coming up with an unique world and religion or whatever was going on there, but I'm still not sure what's going on with some stuff. Universe-specific vocab abounded, with sparse context clues. In order to understand what words or phrases meant, you had to consult the glossary. GLOSSARY! And I'm all for glossaries-- as long as they are supplemental so you can remind yourself what terms mean, not as the only way for you to learn what a Jihad is. So, yeah, it was hard to get through.

It really is not very good. I believe everyone that says it is amazing says that because the have never read it and assume it's good or they think they should say it is awesome because they are confused.  First off it is a fantasy book. There are courts, dukes, emperors and magic. Just because it takes place in the future does not it make it science fiction.  It is incredibly slow. You can add detail and make it exciting.  Dune adds detail in the excitement of a text book.
reviews.title: Meh

reviews.text: Frank Herbert creates a universe with its own religion and society, with characters that have depth (some more than others) but seem often confused. Maybe Herbert does this on purpose because he creates such a rich, detailed and complex universe that the reader (and the characters) can't absorb everything at once, so he omits things or leaves it up to the read/characters to deduce concepts and ideals. I heard and read many great things about this book, but I found it very difficult to read. It didn't become easier as I went along; just the characters and their ideals becoming more easily acclimated. With such complexity, I found that the book suffered in story; it was completely dry to say the least. The characters didn't create any emotional investment, and I honestly didn't care if they lived or died. I found the writing of Herbert to be completely atrocious. I will give Herbert credit: he did put forth effort in creativity, which I believe is the book's greatest achievement.

It was difficult to read for the first half of book (400 pages this half!), I have almost skip this book a few times. Second half was appealing thought. But in summary: I was expecting more from this novel. IMPORTANT: if you are planning to read other books from this series - do not read afterwords by author's son! He is revealing details of the following book... It is like if someone told me in advance what would be my birthday present. Like someone stealing my surprise. Why did he do this?...

although overly verbose and grandiose at times (for the entire first half of the novel, actually) frank herbert does an excellent job of building out a universe that has captivated generations of readers now. it says something that it took me over 4 years to finish (the overwhelming majority of those years spent trying to read the first half of the book), either about me or about herbert's writing style (probably both). this book is a classic and a catalyst for such creativity for good reason though.

The author's overindulgence in technobabble and gibberish adds absolutely nothing to the story. It's as if Frank Hebert is trying to convince the reader that the material is far more exotic than it actually is. The story itself isn't bad but given the buzz behind this call classic I really hoped for more
reviews.title: Overrated

reviews.text: I really enjoyed reading this book. The story was great, the action kept me on edge. I hate to admit I've actually ignored some responsibility to spend extra time reading it. I did find the language challenging. I could not find definitions for words used that fit the context in which he was using them. And many words were made up, or used incorrectly, making comprehension challenging at points. Despite THAT, it was still great. So much better than the movie, which did not do it any justice.

Fascinating concepts and world building, clunky prose and terribly stilted dialogue. FH's writing steadily improves over books 1-3 (Dune, Messiah and Children) and later books in the series are much less of a slog than the first. Absolutely worth reading, this is a phenomenal book given its historical context and is full of great ideas even if it's mechanically lacking.

7-01-2021 There are things I like and things I dislike. The story is ok, but I kind of wish it could be better in some ways. Some of the characters in the book are annoying. Most of the likable characters in this book are killed off. The story is rushed in some parts and slowed in other. The story begins leaving you hoping for something great, but keeps burning all bridges of hope, leaving me a bit disappointing. Hopefully the upcoming movie will help make the story feel a little more exciting.-- The universe the series is set is in is a bit weird, and feels more fantasy.-- Biggest problem I have with is with the author. He seems to have used a thesaurus to find the strangest words he could in place of more simpler ones. Sometimes it gets to the point where the book feels illegible. He also over indulges in the use of the word "Presently" in between dialogue/actions. The book feels unnecessary long, while the story short. Too much unnecessary exposition perhaps?

Great world. Very absorbing.  I can see why this is a sci-fi classic. However, Arrakis is definately the star of this show, and that is a shame. The characters are more like set pieces, illustrating their world's history. It is no surprise that Paul becomes less relatable as he becomes more powerful. The problem is having nobody else to cheer for. Herbert kills off all his underdogs well before the story's climax and does so much foreshadowing that by the time the big battle starts all we have left are an anointed messiah, his disciples, and an assortment of already doomed villains. If the male characters are 2 demensional, the female characters are even flatter. The big twist never comes, the forgone conclusions remain forgone, but the expert world building means this book is still worth reading.
reviews.title: Dune

            "reviewer_name": "Joseph Kreifels II",
            "stars": 4,
            "text": "7-01-2021 There are things I like and things I dislike. The story is ok, but I kind of wish it could be better in some ways. Some of the characters in the book are annoying.             "stars": 4,
            "text": "Great world. Very absorbing.  I can see why this is a sci-fi classic. However, Arrakis is definately the star of this show, and that is a shame. post.description:
All books of a series with position, rating and price, from a `book_series` id (`search`) or the `series.series_id` of `book`.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

country.description: Storefront country (`gl`), ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Default US. Selects currency and availability. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2}$.

language.description: UI language (`hl`), e.g. en_US, en, fr. Default en_US. Selects the language of titles, descriptions and labels. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2}([_-][A-Za-z]{2,4})?$.

series_id.description: Play book series id (`id` query parameter of /store/books/series), e.g. av3XFwAAABC86M. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{6,40}(\.P)?$.

response.description_html:
Frank Herbert’s classic masterpiece—a triumph of the imagination and one of the bestselling science fiction novels of all time.

Set on the desert planet Arrakis, Dune is the story of Paul Atreides—who would become known as Muad'Dib—and of a great family's ambition to bring to fruition mankind's most ancient and unattainable dream.

A stunning blend of adventure and mysticism, environmentalism and politics, Dune won the first Nebula Award, shared the Hugo Award, and formed the basis of what is undoubtedly the grandest epic in science fiction.

post.description:
Details, season list and the episodes of one season (default or chosen by `season_id`) for a Play TV show id from `search`.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

country.description: Storefront country (`gl`), ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Default US. Selects currency and availability. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2}$.

language.description: UI language (`hl`), e.g. en_US, en, fr. Default en_US. Selects the language of titles, descriptions and labels. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2}([_-][A-Za-z]{2,4})?$.

season_id.description: Season whose episodes to return (`season_id` of an entry in `seasons`, e.g. xuqbRMWDkLw). Default: the season the store presents (usually the latest). An id the show does not have is not_found. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{6,40}(\.P)?$.

show_id.description: Play TV show id (`id` query parameter of /store/tv/show), e.g. dfG5FqYlZhc.P. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{6,40}(\.P)?$.

episodes.synopsis_html: On Wallach IX, young Valya Harkonnen promises Mother Superior Raquella that she’ll protect the Sisterhood by putting one of their own on the Imperial Throne. Thirty years later, on Salusa Secundus, Valya works to combat a new threat to her long-awaited plan for a marriage between Princess Ynez-Arat and a young Richese prince.
episodes.title: The Hidden Hand

episodes.synopsis_html: After receiving word about events on Salusa Secundus, Valya brings Theodosia to the Imperial House to help manage the situation. Meanwhile, Desmond makes a confession to Emperor Corrino, Tula reluctantly enlists Lila for a vital mission, and distrust swirls around Keiran Atreides, the sword master for House Corrino.
episodes.title: Two Wolves

episodes.synopsis_html: Following a tragedy, young Tula worries about being accepted despite her family name, while a skeptical Valya struggles with the decision to take the Sisterhood vow. Years later, Valya receives a message that confirms her suspicions, and Tula mourns a loss.
episodes.title: Sisterhood Above All

episodes.synopsis_html: After nearly all the acolytes have the same nightmare, Tula attempts to understand the origins of their disturbing dreams. Meanwhile, on the eve of the great Landsraad meeting, Valya sets her plan in motion to redeem House Harkonnen, Ynez confronts her father about rumors surrounding Desmond, and Kieran conspires to advance a rebel attack that the Sisterhood must try to thwart.
episodes.title: Twice Born

episodes.synopsis_html: As Corrino names a new Bashar, a Sister with deep connections to the Emperor arrives on Salusa Secundus… sending ripples through the Royal House. After receiving a tip, Desmond goes on a warpath to root out the insurgents. Meanwhile, Tula tries to keep her secret project from being discovered by the other Sisters.
episodes.title: In Blood, Truth

episodes.synopsis_html: As Tula contends with the stunning reveal of Desmond’s true identity, the acolytes uncover a devastating long-held secret about the Sisterhood. Meanwhile, Valya executes her plan for Ynez’s escape...which leads to an epic confrontation with an increasingly powerful Desmond.
episodes.title: The High-Handed Enemy

The seasonal baseline to compare a `daily_weather` or `monthly_history` window against (is this season wetter or hotter than normal).

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

geometry.description: GeoJSON (RFC 7946, WGS84, positions as [longitude, latitude] with an optional ignored altitude): a Point, Polygon or MultiPolygon, or a Feature wrapping one. Polygon rings must be closed (first position equals the last). A FeatureCollection is refused (send one place per call), as is a geometry crossing the antimeridian. The object is left open so the program can report the exact failing position as a JSON pointer with a stable code (`ring_not_closed`, `latitude` with a swapped-order hint, `too_large`, `too_many_vertices`, `antimeridian`, `feature_collection`, `unsupported_type`).

parameters.description: POWER climatology parameter codes (`list_parameters` with temporal `climatology`). Default: T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, PRECTOTCORR, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, RH2M, WS2M.

post.description:
Find the code for a quantity (soil wetness, dew point, growing degree days) before asking for its history.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

community.description: POWER user community: AG agroclimatology (default; the units the other functions use), RE renewable energy, SB sustainable buildings.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against code, name and definition. No match is an empty `parameters` list, not an error.

parameters.definition: The amount of water and water vapor present in the soil. Profile indicates the layer from the surface down to the bedrock. Values range from 0 for completely dry conditions to 1 for completely saturated soil.
parameters.name: Profile Soil Moisture

parameters.definition: The amount of water and water vapor available to plants in the root zone, generally considered to be the upper 1 m of soil, expressed as the proportion of water present in a given amount of soil. Values range from 0 for completely dry conditions to 1 for completely saturated soil.
parameters.name: Root Zone Soil Wetness

parameters.definition: The amount of water and water vapor present in the soil. Top indicates the upper 5 cm of soil. Values range from 0 for completely dry conditions to 1 for completely saturated soil.
parameters.name: Surface Soil Wetness

parameters.definition: Total profile soil moisture (0 cm to model bedrock depth).

post.description:
Multi-year seasonal context (how did the last three growing seasons compare) without pulling thousands of daily rows.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

end_year.description: Last year, inclusive; at most 20 years after `start_year`.

geometry.description: GeoJSON (RFC 7946, WGS84, positions as [longitude, latitude] with an optional ignored altitude): a Point, Polygon or MultiPolygon, or a Feature wrapping one. Polygon rings must be closed (first position equals the last). A FeatureCollection is refused (send one place per call), as is a geometry crossing the antimeridian. The object is left open so the program can report the exact failing position as a JSON pointer with a stable code (`ring_not_closed`, `latitude` with a swapped-order hint, `too_large`, `too_many_vertices`, `antimeridian`, `feature_collection`, `unsupported_type`).

parameters.description: POWER monthly parameter codes (`list_parameters` with temporal `monthly`). Default: T2M, PRECTOTCORR, GWETROOT, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN.

sources.name: NASA POWER Monthly and Annual API

post.description:
Start here for any 'what does X cost on Azure in region Y' question: Synapse dedicated SQL pool DWUs, virtual machine sizes, managed disks, storage tiers. Then call get_sku_prices with an `arm_sku_name` or get_meter with a `meter_id` from the results.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

arm_region_name.description: ARM region slug (`armRegionName eq`), e.g. `eastus`, `westeurope`. Unknown regions return an empty result, not an error. Pattern: ^[a-z0-9]{2,40}$.

continuation.description: `continuation` from the previous page (the API's `$skip` offset). Send the same filters again. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,9}$.

currency_code.description: Billing currency (`currencyCode`), ISO 4217. Default USD; EUR verified. Pattern: ^[A-Z]{3}$.

include_savings_plan.description: Request api-version 2023-01-01-preview, which adds `savings_plan` (1 Year / 3 Years) to eligible Consumption rows.

price_type.description: `priceType eq`: Consumption (pay-as-you-go, spot, low priority), DevTestConsumption or Reservation. Omit for all types. Reservation scans over a whole service are expensive and the API answers them with HTTP 429; combine with a product or SKU filter.

primary_meter_region_only.description: Send `meterRegion='primary'`: only rows where the region is the meter's primary region.

product_name.description: Exact `productName`, e.g. `Premium SSD Managed Disks`, `Azure Synapse Analytics Dedicated SQL Pool`. Mutually exclusive with `product_name_contains`.

query.filter: serviceName eq 'Virtual Machines' and armRegionName eq 'eastus' and armSkuName eq 'Standard_D2s_v3' and priceType eq 'Consumption'

reviews.text: Tråkigt att man inte kan betala direkt med kort utan måste gå via klarna.

Rekommenderar inte att handla här. Produkten var bristfälligt och otydligt märkt, vilket ledde till ett felköp. När jag kontaktade butiken vägrade de helt att ta sitt ansvar eller hjälpa till att lösa situationen, trots att dom erkände att informationen saknades. post.description:
Find proteins in a compartment (location Nucleoli, min_reliability Supported), genes enriched in a tissue (tissue liver) or cell type (cell_type hepatocytes), or both at once; then call protein for one gene's full localization and expression, or antibodies for its reagents.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。

cell_type.description: Single cell type name as HPA writes it, case-insensitive and usually plural: hepatocytes, T-cells, cardiomyocytes.

location.description: Subcellular location term exactly as HPA names it.

main_location_only.description: Only genes with location as a main location.

min_reliability.description: Lowest reliability of location to include; default Uncertain (all). Supported keeps Enhanced and Supported.

offset.description: Results to skip; pass the previous page's next_offset.

query.description: Free text (kinase, insulin receptor) or HPA search syntax (protein_class:Transcription factors), ANDed with the other filters. Field values HPA does not know match nothing rather than failing.

specificity.description: RNA specificity categories for tissue or cell_type; default all three. enriched: at least 4x every other tissue or cell type; group_enriched: 4x in a small group; enhanced: 4x the mean.

tissue.description: Tissue name as HPA writes it, case-insensitive: liver, skeletal muscle, cerebral cortex, pancreas.

auction_type.content_html:
Avyttring

Avyttring innebär att en uppdragsgivare har gods de önskar sälja. Det kan t ex vara ett förråd/lager som behövs tömmas, eller att bolaget har strukturerat om och inte behöver kontorsplatser/utrustning/mm längre. Detta skiljer sig från en konkursförsäljning då det är en frivillig försäljning.

delivery_events.notes_html:
Utlämning sker efter tidsbokning på nedan länk.

Boka din tid för utlämning via länken: Bokning 

Tidsbokning skall ske senast 3 dagar efter avslutad auktion.

Hämtning skall ha skett senast 14 dagar efter auktionsavslut annars debiteras du för en lagerhyra för utebliven hämtning.

delivery_terms_html:
Betalning skall vara oss tillhanda innan utlämning kan ske så betala i god tid. Ha gärna fakturakopia till hans när ni kommer till  utlämningstillfället. 
Köparen skall själv på utsatt tid ombesörja hämtning, lastning, ev. nedmontering / emballering av objektet.

Gällande ej hämtade objekt i PS lokaler så har PS rätt att debitera upp 2500 kr ex moms / vecka per objekt

OBS! Eventuell pall och palltillbehör som syns på bilden ingår ej i objektet om detta inte är angett i beskrivningen.
response.description_html:
Svetsmaskin EWM Inverter TIG 200 DC PowerSinus.
Observera: Saknar en fot.
Fungerar efter enklare funktionstest.

shipping.text_html:
Detta objekt går att få fraktat. Du väljer om du önskar frakt i samband med att du lägger ditt bud, så räknas frakten ut automatiskt. 

Om du glömt att välja frakt vid budgivningen, kan du välja till det genom att gå in på "Mina auktion" på ditt konto och klicka i frakt.
OBS! Detta måste göras innan auktionen avslutas

För snabbaste leverans av varan – välj frakt vid budgivningen

Vi skickar vanligtvis din vara inom 5-7 arbetsdagar efter erhållen betalning

shipping_terms_html: OBS! Eventuell pall och palltillbehör som syns på bilden ingår ej i objektet om detta inte är angett i beskrivningen.
terms_html:
Buden är bindande och serviceavgiften debiteras på alla objekt. Eventuella avvikelser från likvärdiga begagnade varor beskrivs under sektionen Anmärkningar i beskrivningen på objektet och därmed ansvarar inte PS för avvikelsen.
Objektet är EJ TESTAT av auktionsfirman om inget annat sägs i objektsbeskrivningen. Objektsbeskrivningen är framtagen efter bästa möjliga förmåga men är ej bindande i detalj.
OBS! Eventuell pall och palltillbehör som syns på bilden ingår ej i objektet om detta inte är angett i beskrivningen.

post.description:
Finding lots by keyword or category on psauction.se, e.g. welding machines, tractors, lots in Skåne, or everything in item type 88 (Verktyg) sorted by highest bid. Use get_filters for item type ids and location slugs, get_item for one lot's full detail.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

hide_ended.description: Exclude closed lots (default true, as the site does).

item_type_ids.description: Item type (category) ids from get_filters, e.g. [88] for Verktyg; several ids are OR-ed.

language.description: Swedish (psauction.se) or English (psauction.com) texts; prices stay in SEK.

limit.description: Page size; 48 is the site default, 144 the largest the API accepts.

location.description: Location slug from get_filters: `SE`, `SE_{county}` or `SE_{county}_{city}`, e.g. `SE_Skåne_Malmö`. Pattern: ^SE(_[^_&=?#/]{1,60}){0,2}$.

only_no_reserve.description: Only lots without a reserve price.

page.description: page

query.description: Free text (`params[freeText]`), e.g. `svets`. Optional: without it the search lists every matching lot.

sort.description: Sort key as the site names it; `real_endtime` is closing soonest.

default.description: Error response; upstream passthrough responses may use provider formats

x-aisa-response-pending.reason: public success response has no authoritative payload declaration

The major features of the project are as follows: • Evaluate alternative cross sections: including lane width, shoulders, bike lane, width of planters, sidewalk width, barrier, and retaining wall type. • Develop criteria and select a preferred alternative. • Develop 30%, 60%, 90%, and final design plans, specifications and cost estimates. • Complete environmental study and permitting • Provide design support during construction • Other improvements and work associated with the sidewalk include, but are not limited to, site preparation, erosion and sediment control, storm drainage system, flow control and water quality facilities, environmentally sensitive area impact mitigation, irrigation, landscaping, channelization, retaining walls, signing, traffic control, and other mitigation as required. The A&E Professional Services Agreement with the successful Consultant firm will conform to all requirements outlined in the Using Consultants chapter of the WSDOT Local Agency Guideline (LAG) Manual. This project is federally funded. This project has zero percent as an FSBE Goal and a voluntary ten percent SBE goal.

bids.description: INTRODUCTION The City of Bellevue (the “City”) is requesting competitive proposals from qualified firms for solid waste collection services within the City Service Area. These services include: residential and commercial garbage, recycling, and organics (yard debris and food scraps) collection, the delivery of garbage to a King County facility per the City’s interlocal agreement, and the processing and marketing of collected recyclables and organics. The initial contract term will be for ten (10) years, from July 1, 2028 to June 30, 2038, with a City option for an extension of up to two (2) years. Terms used in this RFP that are defined in the Contract have the meanings assigned to them therein. Defined terms are applicable to both the singular and plural. EXISTING COLLECTION SYSTEM This section generally describes the existing solid waste collection system operated under the current contract. Carefully review Brief Scope of Services, Attachment “A”, and the draft 2028 Contract (Exhibit A) to determine the scope of operations envisioned under the new Contract. The City’s current contract with Republic Services is available to Proposers upon request. The City of Bellevue has a residential population of approximately 158,000 with approximately 30,800 single-family residential customers and approximately 2,000 multi-family, commercial, and drop-box accounts. The existing collection system is operated under contract with total contractor billings of approximately $37 million in 2025. Garbage collection is voluntary for generators within the City. Single-family Collection Single-family residences are provided weekly garbage collection under a variable rate structure. Under the new contract, Residents will be required to use a contractor-provided garbage cart for basic service, but may use their own containers for extra material. There are approximately 200 single-family residential customers who currently use their own container who will need to transition to a contractor-provided container. Weekly single-family recycling collection is included as part of garbage collection service. Most recyclable materials are placed in the recycling cart except for small appliances and electronics, textiles, and large metal items. Weekly single-family organics (i.e., yard debris and food scraps) collection is also included as part of basic collection services, through the use of 96-gallon carts. Customers may also use Kraft bags and place bundled or boxed materials at the curb as well as rent additional yard debris carts from the Contractor if more than one cart is needed. Customers may set out up to 192 gallons of material per collection, with additional materials accepted for a charge. Non-garbage customers may also subscribe to either or both recycling and organics collection services on a fee-for-service basis. The City has an assignable right to the carts used under the current contract and will assign the ownership of those carts to the Contractor performing services under the new contract. As described in Section 4.1.3 of the draft 2028 Contract (Exhibit A), bill assistance is to be provided to eligible single-family residential customers by the Contractor billing these Customers a reduced percentage of the regular rate for the subscribed service level. The estimated approximate number of eligible Single-family Residential customers and respective rate reductions are: 70% Rate Reduction: 450 Single-family Residential customers (Senior (62+) households at 50% or less of area median income). 35% Rate Reduction: 1,250 Single-family Residential customers (80% or less of area median income). Commercial and Multi-family Collection Multi-family complexes are provided with commercial garbage services, as well as a recycling and organics program that accepts most of the same materials handled by the single-family recycling program. Commercial and Multi-family Complex garbage collection is provided through the use of customer-owned containers and drop-box compactors, as well as contractor-owned carts, detachable containers, and drop-boxes. A range of sizes and collection frequencies are available. Commercial and Multi-family Complex customers currently are provided unlimited recycling and one hundred ninety-two gallons (192) of organics collection per week, via cart service, per garbage container. The City anticipates offering a bill assistance program for multi-family residents. The planned program has a rebate structure and will be funded and directly implemented by the City. There are no rate reductions for the Contractor to implement in regard to this multi-family resident bill assistance program. Disposal All collected garbage is currently delivered to the King County Disposal System per the City/County Interlocal Agreement. Administration The City is responsible for overall solid waste program administration, including managing the collection contract and providing solid waste education and promotion to the public. These activities are funded through an administrative fee and targeted program fees paid to the City, as provided for in the current contract. This system of funding will change under the new contract to a single annual contract fee paid by the contractor to the City. These programs have traditionally been performed through in-house staff or the use of consultants. The solid waste collection contractor is responsible for providing all services, including, but not limited to, customer service, customer billing, distributing public notices about collection service and schedule changes, such as holiday hours, billing adjustment notices, and other service-related communications, as described in the draft 2028 Contract (Exhibit A). RFP Exhibits: Exhibit A provides the draft 2028 Contract, which details all the services expected to be performed by the future contractor. Exhibit B provides 2025 collection data by sector/collection program and customer container counts. Exhibit C provides 2026 rates charged by the current contractor to all sectors of customers. Proposal Form 2A provides a listing of service levels desired under the new Contract and customer counts (where available) for services provided under the current contract. The customer counts provided on Form 2A have been reported by the current contractor, and unless noted otherwise in the instructions or footnotes to Proposal Form 2A, are accurate to the best of the City’s knowledge. RFP OBJECTIVES The City has identified the following objectives for future solid waste services: Alignment with best practices Responsive to community needs: reliability, affordability, user experience Compliance with state laws and local policy Leverage technology and data Along with these objectives, the City also intends to maintain key contract elements, including weekly collection services for single-family residents and an embedded rate structure. The RFP structure and terms, sample base contract, proposed alternatives, and evaluation process are intended to support these objectives.
bids.title: RFP #26039 - Solid Waste Services

bids.description: The City is seeking a highly qualified Design-Build Team with progressive design build experience and strong skills in creativity and collaboration that will engage as critical, integrated team members throughout design and construction of a large-scale landscape project (Phase 1) and leading design of the aquatic center (Phase 2). The Bellevue Airfield Park Project (the 'Project') site is located largely within the I-90 commercial district, near the Lake to Lake Trail and major transportation corridors. The Master Plan for this community park includes trails, wooded picnic areas, a playground, splash pad, flexible lawn play, basketball and pickleball courts, and a new regional aquatic center able to support the demand for recreational and competitive swimming in Bellevue and the broader region. The Apprentice Utilization Requirement for the Project will be 15%.
bids.title: RFQ #26020 - Bellevue Airfield Park Project

It is the responsibility of the contractor to provide all supervision, labor, materials, equipment, disposal, service operations, and expertise required to complete this project for the City of Bellevue in accordance with specifications and site plans. Follow project milestones for ROW landscape inspections checklist, provided at construction pre-con. SEE BID DOCS FOR DETAILED INFOMATION
bids.title: ITQ #26098 - 148th Ave NE, Landscape Renovation

bids.description: This project involves pruning and crown cleaning for up to 168 street trees and removing up to 11 within the northern Bellevue CBD Right-of-Way. Nine trees require only limited dead-wood pruning. Work is time-and-materials with a not-to-exceed limit, and all pruning must follow ISA ANSI A300 and ANSI Z133.1 standards under the supervision of an ISA Certified Arborist, with at least one arborist on-site at all times. Traffic control is required. The City will provide the ROW permit and draft traffic control plans, but the contractor is responsible for all traffic control needed to meet final permit requirements, including any adjustments by the ROW Inspector or needs for Uniformed Police Officers. Contractors must provide all labor, materials, equipment, and disposal necessary to complete the project per City specifications. SEE BID DOCS FOR MORE DETAILS
bids.title: ITQ #26105 - 2026 North CBD Cycle Pruning

Kitchen work includes new equipment and hood and associated structural modifications, roof penetration and installation of hood exhaust, and new cabinets as well as limited electrical, plumbing and mechanical scope. Electrical and plumbing scope require separate trade permit by Contractor. Teen room includes partition demolition, interior door and window reconfiguration and new finishes. Engineer's Estimate Range is $400,000 - $500,000. Attendance at a Pre-Bid site walk/inspection and sign-in by Prime/General Contractors who intend to submit a bid for Work on this project will be held at: 2:00 P.M., October 8th 2026 Crossroads Community Center-16000 NE 10th Bellevue WA 98008

response.abstract: In the past 20 years, sequencing technologies have led to easy access to genomic data from nonmodel organisms in all biological realms. Insect genetic manipulation, however, continues to be a challenge due to various factors, including technical and cost-related issues. Traditional techniques such as microinjection of gene-editing vectors into early stage embryos have been used for arthropod transgenesis and the discovery of Clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats and CRISPR-associated protein (CRISPR-Cas) technologies allowed for targeted mutagenesis and the creation of knockouts or knock-ins in arthropods. Receptor-Mediated Ovary Transduction of Cargo (ReMOT Control) acts as an alternative to embryonic microinjections, which require expensive equipment and extensive hands-on training. ReMOT Control's main advantage is its ease of use coupled with the ability to hypothetically target any vitellogenic species, as injections are administered to the egg-laying adult rather than embryos. After its initial application in the mosquito Aedes aegypti, ReMOT Control has successfully produced mutants not only for mosquitoes but for multiple arthropod species from diverse orders, such as ticks, mites, wasps, beetles, and true bugs, and is being extended to crustaceans, demonstrating the versatility of the technique. In this review, we discuss the current state of ReMOT Control from its proof-of-concept to the advances and challenges in the application across species after 5 years since its development, including novel extensions of the technique such as direct parental (DIPA)-CRISPR.

sections.text: GenBank

GenBank® (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov) is a comprehensive database that contains publicly available nucleotide sequences for almost 260 000 formally described species. These sequences are obtained primarily through submissions from individual laboratories and batch submissions from large-scale sequencing projects, including whole-genome shotgun (WGS) and environmental sampling projects. Most submissions are made using the web-based BankIt or standalone Sequin programs, and GenBank staff assigns accession numbers upon data receipt. Daily data exchange with the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) and the DNA Data Bank of Japan (DDBJ) ensures worldwide coverage. GenBank is accessible through the NCBI Entrez retrieval system, which integrates data from the major DNA and protein sequence databases along with taxonomy, genome, mapping, protein structure and domain information, and the biomedical journal literature via PubMed. BLAST provides sequence similarity searches of GenBank and other sequence databases. Complete bimonthly releases and daily updates of the GenBank database are available by FTP. To access GenBank and its related retrieval and analysis services, begin at the NCBI home page: www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov.
INTRODUCTION

GenBank is a comprehensive public database of nucleotide sequences and supporting bibliographic and biological annotation. GenBank is built and distributed by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), a division of the National Library of Medicine (NLM), located at the campus of the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH) in Bethesda, MD, USA.

NCBI builds GenBank primarily from the submission of sequence data from authors and from the bulk submission of expressed sequence tag (EST), genome survey sequence (GSS), whole-genome shotgun (WGS) and other high-throughput data from sequencing centres. The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office also contributes sequences from issued patents. GenBank participates with the European Molecular Biology Laboratory Nucleotide Sequence Database (EMBL-Bank), part of the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA), and the DNA Data Bank of Japan (DDBJ) as a partner in the International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration (INSDC). The INSDC partners exchange data daily to ensure that a uniform and comprehensive collection of sequence information is available worldwide. NCBI makes the GenBank data available at no cost over the Internet, through FTP and a wide range of web-based retrieval and analysis services.
RECENT DEVELOPMENTS
Submission portal

response.project_description:
Action 6 of the Climate Resilience Planning and Development (CRPD) Action Plan sets out to develop a Wildfire Risk Overlay (map and regulations) in Zoning Bylaw 20001.

The City is to develop a zoning overlay map for Zoning Bylaw 20001 that identifies areas within the wildland urban interface (WUI) where the greatest wildfire risk is present. This map would identify where to apply wildfire risk mitigation zoning regulations to affected properties. The purpose of these zoning regulations is to:

1. Minimize damage and disruption to private and public property in the wildland urban interface due to a wildfire event;
2. Support reducing the cost of rebuilding after a wildfire event; and
3. Ensure the safety of those living in wildfire risk areas.

post.description:
Discover tenders, notices and awards; take `reference_number` into `get_posting`. Use `list_codes`, `list_organizations` and `search_unspsc_codes` to find valid filter values.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

agreement_types.description: Trade agreement codes from list_codes('trade-agreement'), e.g. TA-01 (not applicable), APC-TA-NWPTA.

categories.description: Category codes from list_codes('opportunity-category'): SRV (services), GD (goods), CNST (construction).

cursor.description: Continuation from a previous call's next_cursor (the 0-based page index). Use the same filters and page_size. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,6}$.

delivery_regions.description: Region of delivery display names (facet values or list_codes('region-of-delivery') display values), e.g. 'Edmonton', 'Alberta'.

include_facets.description: Return facet counts (status, category, organization, region, solicitation/opportunity/agreement type, UNSPSC) for the filtered result set. Organization and UNSPSC facets can be several hundred rows.

opportunity_types.description: Posting type codes from list_codes('opportunity-posting-type'): OPEN-COMPETITIVE, LIMITED, NOTICE, INFORMATIONAL, UNDER-THRESHOLD, LIMITED-UNDER-THRESHOLD.

organizations.description: Contracting organization display names exactly as the site spells them (facet values or list_organizations names), e.g. 'City of Calgary'.

post_date_from.description: Earliest post date (inclusive), YYYY-MM-DD, Alberta local date. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

query.description: Free text matched against titles, descriptions and solicitation numbers (e.g. 'wildfire', '935775'). Omit or leave blank to list everything.

query_mode.description: 'standard' is the site's default keyword search; 'enhanced' adds the site's semantic matching (more, looser results).

solicitation_types.description: Solicitation type codes from list_codes('opportunity-solicitation-type'): RFP, ITB, RFQ, NRFP, NOA, ACAN, RFEI, NOI, NOS, NPP, SOW, PQR, RFQual, APC-NA.

sort_by.description: Sort field (the only two the site offers).

statuses.description: Status codes from list_codes('opportunity-status'): OPEN, CLOSED, EVALUATION, SELECTION, AWARD, CANCELLED, UNAWARDABLE, EXPIRED.

unspsc_codes.description: 8-digit UNSPSC codes as strings (segment, family, class or commodity level), e.g. '77000000'. See search_unspsc_codes.

postings.project_description:
The Jackfish Lake Wildfire, Fire Number LCU-003-2023 was approximately 2,553 ha in size.  The wildfire started on May 3rd, 2023, in Athabasca County.  The wildfire encompassed a composite of crown land, private land, grazing leases and forest grazing leases, both within the Forest Protection Area (FPA) and outside the Forest Protection Area (FPA). 

Athabasca County, in its mandate to prevent and suppress wildfires within the County is required to reclaim disturbed forest land caused by wildfire suppression operations. These sites were essential for effective wildfire operations and included fireguards, creek crossings, pipeline crossings, and helipads. Wildfire reclamation is required to prevent or reduce the potential of soil erosion and ensure soil stabilization on or near the fire line. Reclamation of disturbances also promotes the recovery of the disturbed land base for wildlife habitat and vegetative growth. 

The reclamation plan includes the portion of the Jackfish Lake wildfire that is outside the Forest Protection Area (FPA).  The Alberta Government has conducted reclamation activities in the portion of the wildfire withing the Forest Protection Area (FPA).  

Reclamation with mechanical equipment is required to recover the land base to a near natural state. The fireguard travels through trembling aspen and balsam poplar.  White spruce and black spruce are the major coniferous species, with minor compositions tamarack and jack pine, taking advantage of natural clearings when possible. 

The majority of the dozer guards are in higher ground(upland), these areas can be reclaimed in non-frozen dry conditions.  There are stretches of dozer guard classified as upland that may require frozen conditions for access.
postings.title: Athabasca County - Request for Proposal - Jackfish Lake Wildfire Reclamation LCU-003-2023

postings.project_description:
For the primary purpose of wildfire suppression, the Province requires the services of a multiplane Amphibious Airtanker Group supported by one (1) Birddog aircraft. The airtanker group will consist of:

•	A combined Amphibious Airtanker Group capacity of equal to or greater than 10,000 litres with a minimum of two (2) and up to four (4) purposed designed Amphibious Airtankers;  
•	A minimum capacity per Amphibious Airtanker of 3,000 litres;  
•	Each Amphibious Airtanker must be equipped with a compartmentalized or variable/constant flow tank; and 
•	One (1) turbine powered birddog aircraft
All Aircraft must be supported by a fully qualified Aircrew. 
The Province recognizes that there may not be sufficient lead time to acquire, equip, and staff aircraft for the commencement of the 2027 wildfire season. Under these circumstances, the Province may accept the use of one or more Transition Aircraft for a short term, provided the Transition Aircraft are acceptable to the Province. A proposal that includes the use of any Transition Aircraft must be outlined in Attachment #2.

Proponents will supply only aircraft approved by Transport Canada through the issuance of a Canadian Type Certificate or acceptance by Transport Canada of the foreign certificate without issuing its own certificate. Aircraft proposed must meet all Transport Canada legal and regulatory requirements necessary to provide the required Airtanker Services. 

The Contractor will hold a valid license governed by and compliant with the Canadian Transportation Act and a valid Air Operator Certificate (AOC) issued by Transport Canada appropriate to their airtanker operations.

The Province will guarantee 120 days for each Aircraft in each year of the ten year term of the Contract.. There are no guaranteed flying hours during the Core Period.

The Aircraft will be positioned as required throughout Alberta and may be exported outside of the province if required. The Aircraft may be repositioned with minimal notice and for indefinite periods of time.

postings.title: Forestry and Parks - Request for Proposal - Amphibious Airtanker Group

postings.project_description:
Government of Alberta (GoA) Ministries and Agencies are interested in a broad range of satellite imagery and derivative product offerings. This RFP follows several individual pilot projects, including the use of PlanetScope imagery for Machine Learning (ML) derived wetland inventory in collaboration with Ducks Unlimited Canada (DUC) and the Alberta Biodiversity and Monitoring Institute (ABMI), assessment of very-high resolution satellite ortho and stereo images from a variety of sources to seek opportunities for process improvement and optimization related to forestry operations, forest health, and natural resource management, and a Request for Information (RFI) related to products and services of interest to assist with wildfire preparedness and response. 

The RFP will describe known products and services of potential interest to GoA Department or Agency business areas as well as business requirements where access to satellite imagery, satellite derivative products, or processing infrastructure may provide opportunities or solutions. This RFP will be used to secure one (1) or more price-list contracts with commercial satellite imagery vendors, and/or forestry or remote sensing consultants who best fit the stated needs. The contracts will be used on an as-needed and as-funded basis for pilot projects, or to augment operational capabilities, with no minimum work guarantee. The number of contracts to be signed will be at the sole discretion of the Province.
postings.question_submission_details:
Unless otherwise advised by the Contracting Manager, all questions and any form of communication between the Proponents and the Province in relation to this RFP must be submitted in writing to the Contracting Manager using the following email address: epa.pgccontracts@gov.ab.ca. All questions and responses will be documented.

The Proponent has the responsibility to notify the Province, in writing, of any ambiguity, divergence, error, omission, oversight, contradiction, or item subject to more than one interpretation in this RFP, as it is discovered, and to request any instruction, decision, or direction necessary to prepare the Proposal.

Questions or concerns must be communicated in writing to the Contracting Manager at least three (3) Business Days prior to the RFP’s Closing Date and Time.  Questions received after this time will be answered if, in the opinion of the Province, time permits.

Verbal responses to enquiries are not binding on any party.
postings.short_title: ON-DEMAND SATELLITE IMAGERY PRODUCTS AND SERVICES
postings.submission_details:
Proposals must be submitted electronically, via email, in Microsoft Word or Adobe Acrobat format by the RFP Closing Date and Time to the following email address: epa.pgccontracts@gov.ab.ca.  The email subject line should indicate that it is a Proposal and include the RFP number and title.

The complete Proposal should be in one (1) email, including attachments, and should not be larger than 25MB to facilitate receipt by the Province.  If multiple emails are required to accommodate attachment sizes, the emails should provide clear instructions on how the Proposal is to be integrated (e.g. 1 of 3, 2 of 3, 3 of 3).

The official time and date of receipt of the Proposal will be determined by the email received time as recorded by the Government of Alberta’s email server.  Proponents should be aware that, prior to such electronic delivery, incoming emails are subject to consistency checks and antivirus scans, which process can take several minutes or longer to complete.  The Province will not be responsible for failures (technical or otherwise) that may result in a Proposal not being received prior to the RFP Closing Date and Time.
If the Proposal cannot be opened after reasonable efforts are made by the Province, the Proposal will be rejected.

The Proposal should be secured against accidental modification by the Province while being searchable and printable in its entirety.

Proposals must be received before 14:01:00 Alberta Time on the RFP Closing Date, or the Proposal will be rejected.

Proposals received after the RFP Closing Date and Time will be deleted.
postings.title: Environment and Protected Areas - Request for Proposal - ON-DEMAND SATELLITE IMAGERY PRODUCTS AND SERVICES

post.description:
Incrementally track everything that changes on PyPI: poll with the last seen serial. Upstream serves up to 50 000 events per call; `limit` windows them and `next_serial` resumes.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

since_serial.description: Return events with a serial greater than this (use `next_serial` or `head_serial` from a previous call).

default.description: Error response; upstream passthrough responses may use provider formats

vulnerabilities.details:
### Impact

Due to a URL parsing issue, Requests releases prior to 2.32.4 may leak .netrc credentials to third parties for specific maliciously-crafted URLs.

### Workarounds
For older versions of Requests, use of the .netrc file can be disabled with `trust_env=False` on your Requests Session ([docs](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/#requests.Session.trust_env)).

### References
https://github.com/psf/requests/pull/6965
https://seclists.org/fulldisclosure/2025/Jun/2

### Impact
The `requests.utils.extract_zipped_paths()` utility function uses a predictable filename when extracting files from zip archives into the system temporary directory. If the target file already exists, it is reused without validation. A local attacker with write access to the temp directory could pre-create a malicious file that would be loaded in place of the legitimate one.

### Affected usages
**Standard usage of the Requests library is not affected by this vulnerability.** Only applications that call `extract_zipped_paths()` directly are impacted.

### Remediation
Upgrade to at least Requests 2.33.0, where the library now extracts files to a non-deterministic location.

If developers are unable to upgrade, they can set `TMPDIR` in their environment to a directory with restricted write access.

### Impact

Due to a URL parsing issue, Requests releases prior to 2.32.4 may leak .netrc credentials to third parties for specific maliciously-crafted URLs.

### Workarounds
For older versions of Requests, use of the .netrc file can be disabled with `trust_env=False` on your Requests Session ([docs](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/#requests.Session.trust_env)).

### References
https://github.com/psf/requests/pull/6965
https://seclists.org/fulldisclosure/2025/Jun/2

Requests is a HTTP library. Prior to version 2.33.0, the `requests.utils.extract_zipped_paths()` utility function uses a predictable filename when extracting files from zip archives into the system temporary directory. If the target file already exists, it is reused without validation. A local attacker with write access to the temp directory could pre-create a malicious file that would be loaded in place of the legitimate one. Standard usage of the Requests library is not affected by this vulnerability. Only applications that call `extract_zipped_paths()` directly are impacted. Starting in version 2.33.0, the library extracts files to a non-deterministic location. If developers are unable to upgrade, they can set `TMPDIR` in their environment to a directory with restricted write access.

biography.blurb: Based in Los Angeles, James Axon is a musically studied and deep-digging DJ known for introducing dance floors to new sounds and new music, equally often through cutting-edge new releases as through the forgotten and obscure gems of the past.
biography.content:
James Axon is a DJ, musician, and creator of the LA-based queer underground party Planet Love, as well as a resident on Dublab with his radio show Hearing Color. A lifelong pianist turned obsessive record collector, James Axon approaches DJing as an extension of musicianship. Before falling into house and techno, he spent years in bands and orchestral ensembles, a background that still shapes the way he thinks about rhythm, harmony, and structuring his sets compositionally. 

As a keyboardist and musician, he has collaborated with Seven Davis Jr. and Massimiliano Pagliara, and as a DJ has shared lineups with the likes of Octo Octa, Eris Drew,  Avalon Emerson,The Blessed Madonna, Derrick Carter, Paramida, Peach, Moxie, Alex Kassian, Zombies in Miami, Jennifer Loveless, Sally C, Tornado Wallace, Perel, Eli Escobar, Paurro, and more. 

His sets drift seamlessly between house, techno, italo, electro, disco, and breaks, guided by an expansive taste shaped by pioneering artists like Aphex Twin, Kraftwerk, Giorgio Moroder, Jeff Mills, Laurent Garnier, Andrew Weatherall, and Francois Kevorkian. His sets are always colorful, eclectic, and intuitively reflective of the setting -- whether playing cosmic disco in an intimate loft or hypnotic techno in a dark foggy warehouse, he still finds a sound that is distinctly James Axon: melodic and synth-heavy, driving and dreamy.

area_id.description: RA area id from `areas` (8 New York City, 34 Berlin, 13 London, 1 Sydney). RA stores area ids as 16-bit integers.

date_from.description: First local listing date, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: today (UTC). Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

date_to.description: Last local listing date, inclusive. Default: `date_from` + 7 days; at most 366 days after `date_from`. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

page.description: 1-based page; use `next_page` from the previous response.

query.description: Keyword matched against event titles within the area and window.

sort.description: `date`: RA's listing order (listing date, then relevance score, then title). `popularity`: most attending first. Default `date`.

response.content:
# Incident Report: September 30, 2026: Domain Routing Disruption

On September 30, 2026, domains hosted on Railway returned 404 not found errors for new connections for a five minute period for all customers.

While rolling out a change to our distributed routing control plane, the new deployment didn’t wait for the schema updates needed to support new functionality. Our distributed routing control plane is the system that tells our origin proxies how to route user requests to the workloads behind every domain.

Because of this mismatch, route lookups failed, and any attempt to reach a domain served by Railway-hosted workloads returned an error. During the incident period, our origin proxies treated each failed lookup as if "this domain doesn't exist" instead of falling back to the last route it knew.

After five minutes of the system automatically reconciling to the intended working state - it restored most traffic; then routing recovered on its own as soon as the schema update finished.

## Impact

On September 30, 2026, between roughly 07:35 and 07:40 UTC, new connections to domains hosted on Railway (which include custom domains and `*.up.railway.app` domains) returned HTTP 404 in all regions.

Public access and some private networking lookups between services failed during this window. User service uptime was not impacted, only access as workloads kept running throughout we are able to confirm that no data was lost.

## Incident Timeline

*All times are UTC on September

response.content:
# Vercel Integration, Codespaces, and CLI

# Vercel Integration

Railway can now hook into Vercel to provide your production and preview deploys with access to your railway environments.

This means that if you add the Postgres plugin to your Railway project, we'll update Vercel with a `DATABASE_URL` connection string, accessible via envvars.

Just tell us which Railway environment to sync, and we'll do the rest.

![](https://cms.railway.com/media/c224041b2f3444b2770b7fa21911062e99f140851a49dd7607f8fa38a13958da.gif)

This is the first of many integrations to come. We already have a few more
planned, but if you'd like a specific integration, please join the
[Discord](https://discord.gg/xAm2w6g) and let us know.

# Codespaces

Railway is now fully compatible with [Github Codespaces](https://github.com/features/codespaces).

Codespaces allows you to
develop entirely in the cloud. Use Railway to connect to your favorite infrastructure, and deploy straight from codespaces with `railway up`.

![](https://cms.railway.com/media/f2ea452147b015e892a12a9fa43299edca98aa702cb0001aff55c641bb4b5fb9.png)

Above is our [Railway Images](https://github.com/railwayapp/railway-images) starter, which uses Prisma and Railway to host a simple image grid, using Railway's Postgres as a backend. Live now on [Vercel](https://railway-images-vercel.vercel.app/)

# Improved UI/UX of CLI

The CLI comes new and improved in this update, featuring:

- 🌈 Added colours
- 🚨 Better error messages
- 🌍 Support for `railway login` in SSH or codespaces terminals

response.description: Pay only for what your app uses, by the second. No overprovisioning, no idle markup.

faq.answer: Hobby is for indie hackers and developers to build and deploy personal projects. Pro is for professional developers and their teams shipping to production. Enterprise is for dev teams building and deploying production applications with large replica size, SLA, and/or compliance needs.
faq.question: Which plan is right for me?

faq.answer: If you do not already have a Railway account, you can sign up for a free Trial by clicking Login on railway.com.
faq.question: How do I get started with the free Trial?

faq.answer: When you sign up for the free Trial, you will receive a one-time grant of $5 in credits that you can use to try out Railway. The credits will be applied towards any usage on the platform and expire in 30 days. If you upgrade to a plan while you still have a credit balance from the trial, the remaining balance will carry over to your new plan.
faq.question: How does the Trial work?

faq.answer: Your Hobby plan subscription includes $5 of usage per month. If your total usage at the end of your billing period is $5 or less, you will not be charged extra for usage. If your total usage exceeds $5 in any given billing period, you will be charged total usage.
faq.question: How does the Hobby plan included usage work?

faq.answer: Included usage is reset at the end of every billing cycle and does not accumulate over time.
faq.question: Does included usage on Hobby accumulate?

faq.answer: Sandboxes run on Railway's VM primitive and bill on VM rates: $50 per GB of memory per month and $50 per vCPU per month, metered per second, plus $0.05 per GB of egress. You pay for the CPU a sandbox actually uses and the memory it holds while running, not for wall-clock uptime, so a sandbox waiting on a model or a user costs almost nothing. Destroyed sandboxes cost nothing, and an idle timeout destroys forgotten ones automatically. Sandbox usage draws from the same included credit as the rest of your plan.
faq.question: How are sandboxes billed?

faq.answer: When you make a payment, you will receive an email with your invoice and receipt attached. You can also find your billing history in Account > Billing.
faq.question: How can I get a receipt?

faq.answer: Head to Account > Billing and click 'Manage Subscription'. From there, you can update your billing information, including billing address and Tax ID.
faq.question: How to add company details on my invoice?

faq.answer: Railway accepts credit cards for plan subscriptions and usage. We support invoice payments for customers on the Enterprise plan.
faq.question: What payment methods are accepted?

faq.answer: Yes. As a new Railway user, you can sign up for a free Trial. You will receive a one-time grant of $5 to use on resources.
faq.question: Can I try Railway without a credit card?

faq.answer: You can upgrade any time, and when you do, you will get to the features of your new plan, as well as access to more powerful resources, immediately. When you downgrade, the changes will take effect at the beginning of your next billing cycle.
faq.question: Can I upgrade or downgrade at any time?

faq.answer: When you cancel your subscription, if you're on Hobby or Pro, your plan will remain active through the end of your current billing period, and any usage will be charged at the end of the period. If you are on the Hobby plan and using prepaid credits as your payment method, your subscription will be canceled immediately and any credit balance you may have will be forfeited.
faq.question: What happens when I cancel my subscription?

response.title: Railway Pricing

This page is a navigational summary of Railway's Terms of Service. **The authoritative, binding version is the HTML page at https://railway.com/legal/terms.** Agents should consult that page (or this page rendered with `Accept: text/html`) for the full legal text before drawing any conclusion about rights and obligations.

## What the Terms cover

- **Acceptance.** Using Railway services means you accept these Terms and the related policies linked from them.
- **Account & access.** Your responsibilities for the security of your Railway account, credentials, and any users you invite.
- **Services & subscriptions.** The compute, storage, networking, and database services Railway provides, plus billing terms for hobby, pro, and enterprise plans.
- **Acceptable use.** What you can and cannot run on Railway. See https://railway.com/legal/acceptable-use for the full list of prohibited activities.
- **Customer content & data.** Ownership of content you upload, the license you grant Railway to host and serve it, and Railway's confidentiality and security commitments.
- **Privacy.** How Railway handles personal data. See https://railway.com/legal/privacy.

- **Term & termination.** How either party can end the relationship and what happens to your data.

latest_update.message:
Builds have resumed for all workspaces and are completing normally. This incident is now resolved.

If you triggered a deploy, pushed to GitHub, or restarted a service while builds were paused, please trigger it again. Those were not queued during the pause and will not start on their own. Cron jobs scheduled during the pause did not run, and will continue from their next scheduled time.

We're sorry for the disruption

The issue affecting build times in US West has been resolved. Build times have returned to normal and the queue has cleared.

We apologize for any inconvenience. If you continue to experience issues, please contact support at https://station.railway.com.

cursor.description: A `cursor` from a previous `daily` response: re-reads that station-month and fails with invalid_input/publication_changed if the rows no longer hash the same.

month.description: Calendar month `YYYY-MM`, 2000-01 to the current month. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}$.

station.description: Four-character RAWS station code, e.g. `MNIN`. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9]{4}$.

units.description: `M` metric (default: °C, m/s, mm, mb, kWh/m²) or `E` English.

post.description:
Find PDB entries for a protein, gene product, organism, ligand or method; join from UniProt with `uniprot_accession` or from a drug with `ligand`. Then call `structure` for chains, ligands, citation and download links.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

ligand.description: Structures containing this Chemical Component Dictionary id as a non-polymer ligand, e.g. `STI` (imatinib), `HEM`, `ATP`. Look ids up with the `ligand` function. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,5}$.

max_resolution.description: Best resolution cutoff in ångströms (≤). Entries without a resolution (most NMR) are excluded when set.

offset.description: Number of hits to skip; pass the previous page's `next_offset`.

organism.description: Source organism scientific name, matched case-insensitively against the NCBI taxonomy lineage of every polymer entity, so `Escherichia coli` includes its strains and `Mammalia` includes every mammal.

query.description: Full-text search over titles, descriptions, keywords, organisms, ligand names, citations and annotations, e.g. `imatinib`, `spike glycoprotein`, `CRISPR Cas9`.

released_after.description: Initial release on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

released_before.description: Initial release on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

sort.description: `relevance` (search score), `newest` (initial release date, newest first) or `resolution` (best first, entries without a resolution last).

uniprot_accession.description: Structures with a polymer entity mapped to this UniProtKB accession (SIFTS/RCSB reference sequence mapping), e.g. `P69905` for human hemoglobin alpha. Pattern: ^([OPQopq][0-9][A-Za-z0-9]{3}[0-9]|[A-NR-Za-nr-z][0-9]([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{2}[0-9]){1,2})$.

response.content:
# Sync Phases and Waves

Sync phases and hooks define when resources are applied such as before or after the main sync operation. This makes it possible to define jobs, or any other resource to run or be applied in any specific order.

Argo CD has the following hook types:

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `PreSync` | Executes prior to the application of the manifests. |
| `Sync` | Executes after all `PreSync` hooks completed and were successful, at the same time as the application of the manifests. |
| `Skip` | Indicates to Argo CD to skip the application of the manifest. |
| `PostSync` | Executes after all `Sync` hooks completed and were successful, a successful application, and all resources in a `Healthy` state. |
| `SyncFail` | Executes when the sync operation fails. |
| `PreDelete` | Executes before Application resources are deleted. Only runs when the entire Application is being deleted, not during normal sync operations (even with pruning enabled. ) |
| `PostDelete` | Executes after all Application resources are deleted. *Available starting in v2.10.* |

Adding the argocd.argoproj.io/hook annotation to a resource will assign it to a specific phase. During a Sync operation, Argo CD will apply the resource during the appropriate phase of the deployment. Hooks can be any type of Kubernetes resource kind, but tend to be Pod, Job or Argo Workflows. Multiple hooks can be specified as a comma separated list.

## How phases work?

Argo CD will respect resources assigned to different phases, during a sync operation Argo CD will do the following:

1. Apply all the resources marked as PreSync hooks. If any of them fails the whole sync process will stop and will be marked as failed
2. Apply all the resources marked as Sync hooks. If any of them fails the whole sync process will be marked as failed. Hooks marked with SyncFail will also run
3. Apply all the resources marked as PostSync hooks. If any of them fails the whole sync process will be marked as failed.

Hooks marked with Skip will not be applied.

Here is a graphical overview of the sync process:

![phases](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/how_phases_work.png)

You can use this simple lifecycle method in various scenarios. For example you can run an essential check as a PreSync hook. If it fails then the whole sync operation will stop preventing the deployment from taking place. In a similar manner you can run smoke tests as PostSync hooks. If they succeed you know that your application has passed the validation. If they fail then the whole deployment will be marked as failed and Argo CD can then notify you in order to take further actions.

Hooks do not run during a selective sync operation. During the SyncFail phase, hooks can be used for cleanup and other housekeeping tasks. If a SyncFail hook itself fails, Argo CD does not take any additional action beyond marking the overall operation as failed.

During pruning, the wave order is reversed from the creation order. Resources in higher waves are pruned first. If pruning any resource in a wave fails, the operation is marked as failed, and resources in lower waves are not processed. This ensures that dependent resources are deleted in the correct order.

## Hook lifecycle and cleanup

Argo CD offers several methods to clean up hooks and decide how much history will be kept for previous runs. In the most basic case you can use the argocd.argoproj.io/hook-delete-policy to decide when a hook will be deleted. This can take the following values:

| Policy | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `HookSucceeded` | The hook resource is deleted when the sync succeeds. For completion-based hooks such as `Job` or `Workflow`, this typically happens after the hook completes successfully. |
| `HookFailed` | The hook resource is deleted after the hook failed. |
| `BeforeHookCreation` | Any existing hook resource is deleted before the new one is created (since v1.3). It is meant to be used with `/metadata/name`. |

Note that if no deletion policy is specified, Argo CD will automatically assume `BeforeHookCreation` rules.

When Helm hook annotations are mapped onto Argo CD hooks, delete-policy evaluation still follows Argo CD sync phases and sync result semantics rather than Helm's per-hook-event lifecycle. For example, a `PreSync` resource mapped from Helm may remain available until later phases finish, and passive resources such as `ServiceAccount` do not have a completion state like `Job` or `Workflow`.

## PreDelete and PostDelete Hooks

### PreDelete Hooks

PreDelete hooks execute before an Application and its resources are deleted. They run only during Application deletion (e.g., `kubectl delete application` or `argocd app delete`), not during normal sync operations, even when pruning is enabled. **Behavior:**

1. When an Application is deleted, Argo CD checks for PreDelete hooks defined in the Application's manifests
2. If PreDelete hooks exist, they are created and executed before any Application resources are deleted
3. Argo CD waits for all PreDelete hooks to reach a Healthy state before proceeding with deletion
4. Once all PreDelete hooks complete successfully, they are cleaned up and the Application resources are deleted

**Failure Handling:**

If a PreDelete hook fails (e.g., a Job fails or a Pod crashes), the Application deletion is blocked:

- The Application will remain in a deleting state with a `DeletionError` condition
- Application resources will not be deleted until the hook succeeds
- The user can fix the failing hook by updating its manifest in the git repository
- After fixing the hook, Argo CD will automatically retry the deletion on the next reconciliation
- Alternatively, the user can manually delete the failing hook resource to allow deletion to proceed

### PostDelete Hooks

PostDelete hooks execute after all Application resources have been deleted. They are useful for cleanup operations, notifications, or removing external resources.

**Behavior:**

1. Application resources are deleted first
2. Once all Application resources are fully removed, PostDelete hooks are created and executed
3. Argo CD waits for all PostDelete hooks to reach a Healthy state
4. Once all PostDelete hooks complete successfully, they are cleaned up and the Application is fully removed

**Failure Handling:**

If a PostDelete hook fails:

- The Application is already deleted from the cluster, but the Application CR remains with a `DeletionError` condition
- The user can fix the failing hook by updating its manifest in the git repository
- After fixing the hook, Argo CD will automatically retry on the next reconciliation
- Alternatively, the user can manually delete the failing hook resource to complete the Application deletion

## How sync waves work?

Argo CD also offers an alternative method of changing the sync order of resources. These are sync waves. They are defined by the argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave annotation. The value is an integer that defines the ordering (ArgoCD will start deploying from the lowest number and finish with the highest number).

Hooks and resources are assigned to wave 0 by default. The wave can be negative, so you can create a wave that runs before all other resources.

When a sync operation takes place, Argo CD will:

1. Order all resources according to their wave (lowest to highest)
2. Apply the resources according to the resulting sequence

There is currently a delay between each sync wave in order to give other controllers a chance to react to the spec change that was just applied. This also prevents Argo CD from assessing resource health too quickly (against the stale object), causing hooks to fire prematurely. The current delay between each sync wave is 2 seconds and can be configured via the environment variable ARGOCD\_SYNC\_WAVE\_DELAY.

## Combining Sync waves and hooks

While you can use sync waves on their own, for maximum flexibility you can combine them with hooks. This way you can use sync phases for coarse grained ordering and sync waves for defining the exact order of a resource within an individual phase.

![waves](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/how_waves_work.png)

When Argo CD starts a sync, it orders the resources in the following precedence:

1. The phase
2. The wave they are in (lower values first)
3. By kind (e.g. namespaces first and then other Kubernetes resources, followed by custom resources)
4. By name

Once the order is defined:

1. First Argo CD determines the number of the first wave to apply. This is the first number where any resource is out-of-sync or unhealthy.
2. It applies resources in that wave.
3. It repeats this process until all phases and waves are in-sync and healthy.

Because an application can have resources that are unhealthy in the first wave, it may be that the app can never get to healthy.

## How Do I Configure Phases?

Pre-sync and post-sync can only contain hooks. Apply the hook annotation:

```
metadata:
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PreSync
```

[Read more about hooks](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/resource_hooks/).

## How Do I Configure Waves?

Specify the wave using the following annotation:

```
metadata:
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "5"
```

Hooks and resources are assigned to wave zero by default. The wave can be negative, so you can create a wave that runs before all other resources.

## Examples

### Send message to Slack when sync completes

The following example uses the Slack API to send a Slack message when sync completes:

```
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  generateName: app-slack-notification-
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PostSync
    argocd.argoproj.io/hook-delete-policy: HookSucceeded
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: slack-notification
          image: curlimages/curl
          command:
            - curl
            - '-X'
            - POST
            - '--data-urlencode'
            - >-
              payload={"channel": "#somechannel", "username": "hello", "text":
              "App Sync succeeded", "icon_emoji": ":ghost:"}
            - 'https://hooks.slack.com/services/...'
      restartPolicy: Never
  backoffLimit: 2
```

### Initialize or migrate a database

The following example runs a db initialization/migration command before the main sync operation (also in wave -1):

```
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: db-migrate
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PreSync
    argocd.argoproj.io/hook-delete-policy: HookSucceeded
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: '-1'
spec:
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 360
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: postgresql-client
          image: 'my-postgres-data:11.5'
          imagePullPolicy: Always
          env:
            - name: PGPASSWORD
              value: admin
            - name: POSTGRES_HOST
              value: my_postgresql_db
          command:
            - psql
            - '-h=my_postgresql_db'
            - '-U postgres'
            - '-f preload.sql'
      restartPolicy: Never
  backoffLimit: 1
```

### Work around ArgoCD sync failure

Upgrading ingress-nginx controller (managed by helm) with ArgoCD 2.x sometimes fails to work resulting in:

| . | . |
| --- | --- |
| OPERATION | Sync |
| PHASE | Running |
| MESSAGE | waiting for completion of hook batch/Job/ingress-nginx-admission-create |

| . | . |
| --- | --- |
| KIND | batch/v1/Job |
| NAMESPACE | ingress-nginx |
| NAME | ingress-nginx-admission-create |
| STATUS | Running |
| HOOK | PreSync |
| MESSAGE | Pending deletion |

To work around this, a helm user can add:

```
ingress-nginx:
  controller:
    admissionWebhooks:
      annotations:
        argocd.argoproj.io/hook: Skip
```

Which results in a successful sync.
