accepted_answer.body_html:
To understand what yield does, you must understand what generators are. And before you can understand generators, you must understand iterables.

Iterables

When you create a list, you can read its items one by one. Reading its items one by one is called iteration:

>>> mylist = [1, 2, 3]
>>> for i in mylist:
...    print(i)
1
2
3

mylist is an iterable. When you use a list comprehension, you create a list, and so an iterable:

>>> mylist = [x*x for x in range(3)]
>>> for i in mylist:
...    print(i)
0
1
4

Everything you can use "for... in..." on is an iterable; lists, strings, files...

These iterables are handy because you can read them as much as you wish, but you store all the values in memory and this is not always what you want when you have a lot of values.

Generators

Generators are iterators, a kind of iterable you can only iterate over once. Generators do not store all the values in memory, they generate the values on the fly:

>>> mygenerator = (x*x for x in range(3))
>>> for i in mygenerator:
...    print(i)
0
1
4

It is just the same except you used () instead of []. BUT, you cannot perform for i in mygenerator a second time since generators can only be used once: they calculate 0, then forget about it and calculate 1, and end after calculating 4, one by one.

Yield

yield is a keyword that is used like return, except the function will return a generator.

>>> def create_generator():
...    mylist = range(3)
...    for i in mylist:
...        yield i*i
...
>>> mygenerator = create_generator() # create a generator
>>> print(mygenerator) # mygenerator is an object!
<generator object create_generator at 0xb7555c34>
>>> for i in mygenerator:
...     print(i)
0
1
4

Here it's a useless example, but it's handy when you know your function will return a huge set of values that you will only need to read once.

To master yield, you must understand that when you call the function, the code you have written in the function body does not run. The function only returns the generator object, this is a bit tricky.

Then, your code will continue from where it left off each time for uses the generator.

Now the hard part:

The first time the for calls the generator object created from your function, it will run the code in your function from the beginning until it hits yield, then it'll return the first value of the loop. Then, each subsequent call will run another iteration of the loop you have written in the function and return the next value. This will continue until the generator is considered empty, which happens when the function runs without hitting yield. That can be because the loop has come to an end, or because you no longer satisfy an "if/else".

Your code explained

Generator:

# Here you create the method of the node object that will return the generator
def _get_child_candidates(self, distance, min_dist, max_dist):

    # Here is the code that will be called each time you use the generator object:

    # If there is still a child of the node object on its left
    # AND if the distance is ok, return the next child
    if self._leftchild and distance - max_dist < self._median:
        yield self._leftchild

    # If there is still a child of the node object on its right
    # AND if the distance is ok, return the next child
    if self._rightchild and distance + max_dist >= self._median:
        yield self._rightchild

    # If the function arrives here, the generator will be considered empty
    # There are no more than two values: the left and the right children

Caller:

# Create an empty list and a list with the current object reference
result, candidates = list(), [self]

# Loop on candidates (they contain only one element at the beginning)
while candidates:

    # Get the last candidate and remove it from the list
    node = candidates.pop()

    # Get the distance between obj and the candidate
    distance = node._get_dist(obj)

    # If the distance is ok, then you can fill in the result
    if distance <= max_dist and distance >= min_dist:
        result.extend(node._values)

    # Add the children of the candidate to the candidate's list
    # so the loop will keep running until it has looked
    # at all the children of the children of the children, etc. of the candidate
    candidates.extend(node._get_child_candidates(distance, min_dist, max_dist))

return result

This code contains several smart parts:

  • The loop iterates on a list, but the list expands while the loop is being iterated. It's a concise way to go through all these nested data even if it's a bit dangerous since you can end up with an infinite loop. In this case, candidates.extend(node._get_child_candidates(distance, min_dist, max_dist)) exhausts all the values of the generator, but while keeps creating new generator objects which will produce different values from the previous ones since it's not applied on the same node.

  • The extend() method is a list object method that expects an iterable and adds its values to the list.

Usually, we pass a list to it:

>>> a = [1, 2]
>>> b = [3, 4]
>>> a.extend(b)
>>> print(a)
[1, 2, 3, 4]

But in your code, it gets a generator, which is good because:

  1. You don't need to read the values twice.
  2. You may have a lot of children and you don't want them all stored in memory.

And it works because Python does not care if the argument of a method is a list or not. Python expects iterables so it will work with strings, lists, tuples, and generators! This is called duck typing and is one of the reasons why Python is so cool. But this is another story, for another question...

You can stop here, or read a little bit to see an advanced use of a generator:

Controlling a generator exhaustion

>>> class Bank(): # Let's create a bank, building ATMs
...    crisis = False
...    def create_atm(self):
...        while not self.crisis:
...            yield "$100"
>>> hsbc = Bank() # When everything's ok the ATM gives you as much as you want
>>> corner_street_atm = hsbc.create_atm()
>>> print(corner_street_atm.next())
$100
>>> print(corner_street_atm.next())
$100
>>> print([corner_street_atm.next() for cash in range(5)])
['$100', '$100', '$100', '$100', '$100']
>>> hsbc.crisis = True # Crisis is coming, no more money!
>>> print(corner_street_atm.next())
<type 'exceptions.StopIteration'>
>>> wall_street_atm = hsbc.create_atm() # It's even true for new ATMs
>>> print(wall_street_atm.next())
<type 'exceptions.StopIteration'>
>>> hsbc.crisis = False # The trouble is, even post-crisis the ATM remains empty
>>> print(corner_street_atm.next())
<type 'exceptions.StopIteration'>
>>> brand_new_atm = hsbc.create_atm() # Build a new one to get back in business
>>> for cash in brand_new_atm:
...    print cash
$100
$100
$100
$100
$100
$100
$100
$100
$100
...

Note: For Python 3, useprint(corner_street_atm.__next__()) or print(next(corner_street_atm))

It can be useful for various things like controlling access to a resource.

Itertools, your best friend

The itertools module contains special functions to manipulate iterables. Ever wish to duplicate a generator? Chain two generators? Group values in a nested list with a one-liner? Map / Zip without creating another list?

Then just import itertools.

An example? Let's see the possible orders of arrival for a four-horse race:

>>> horses = [1, 2, 3, 4]
>>> races = itertools.permutations(horses)
>>> print(races)
<itertools.permutations object at 0xb754f1dc>
>>> print(list(itertools.permutations(horses)))
[(1, 2, 3, 4),
 (1, 2, 4, 3),
 (1, 3, 2, 4),
 (1, 3, 4, 2),
 (1, 4, 2, 3),
 (1, 4, 3, 2),
 (2, 1, 3, 4),
 (2, 1, 4, 3),
 (2, 3, 1, 4),
 (2, 3, 4, 1),
 (2, 4, 1, 3),
 (2, 4, 3, 1),
 (3, 1, 2, 4),
 (3, 1, 4, 2),
 (3, 2, 1, 4),
 (3, 2, 4, 1),
 (3, 4, 1, 2),

accepted_answer.body_markdown:
To understand what [`yield`] does, you must understand what *[generators]* are. And before you can understand generators, you must understand *[iterables]*.

Iterables
---------

When you create a list, you can read its items one by one. Reading its items one by one is called iteration:

    >>> mylist = [1, 2, 3]
    >>> for i in mylist:
    ...    print(i)
    1
    2
    3

`mylist` is an *iterable*. When you use a list comprehension, you create a list, and so an iterable:

    >>> mylist = [x*x for x in range(3)]
    >>> for i in mylist:
    ...    print(i)
    0
    1
    4

Everything you can use "`for... in...`" on is an iterable; `lists`, `strings`, files...

These iterables are handy because you can read them as much as you wish, but you store all the values in memory and this is not always what you want when you have a lot of values.

Generators
----------

Generators are *[iterators]*, a kind of iterable **you can only iterate over once**. Generators do not store all the values in memory, **they generate the values on the fly**:

    >>> mygenerator = (x*x for x in range(3))
    >>> for i in mygenerator:
    ...    print(i)
    0
    1
    4

It is just the same except you used `()` instead of `[]`. BUT, you **cannot** perform `for i in mygenerator` a second time since generators can only be used once: they calculate 0, then forget about it and calculate 1, and end after calculating 4, one by one.

Yield
-----

`yield` is a keyword that is used like `return`, except the function will return a generator.

    >>> def create_generator():
    ...    mylist = range(3)
    ...    for i in mylist:
    ...        yield i*i
    ...
    >>> mygenerator = create_generator() # create a generator
    >>> print(mygenerator) # mygenerator is an object!
    <generator object create_generator at 0xb7555c34>
    >>> for i in mygenerator:
    ...     print(i)
    0
    1
    4

Here it's a useless example, but it's handy when you know your function will return a huge set of values that you will only need to read once.

To master `yield`, you must understand that **when you call the function, the code you have written in the function body does not run.** The function only returns the generator object, this is a bit tricky.

Then, your code will continue from where it left off each time `for` uses the generator.

Now the hard part:

The first time the `for` calls the generator object created from your function, it will run the code in your function from the beginning until it hits `yield`, then it'll return the first value of the loop. Then, each subsequent call will run another iteration of the loop you have written in the function and return the next value. This will continue until the generator is considered empty, which happens when the function runs without hitting `yield`. That can be because the loop has come to an end, or because you no longer satisfy an `"if/else"`.

---

Your code explained
-------------------

*Generator:*

    # Here you create the method of the node object that will return the generator
    def _get_child_candidates(self, distance, min_dist, max_dist):

        # Here is the code that will be called each time you use the generator object:

        # If there is still a child of the node object on its left
        # AND if the distance is ok, return the next child
        if self._leftchild and distance - max_dist < self._median:
            yield self._leftchild

        # If there is still a child of the node object on its right
        # AND if the distance is ok, return the next child
        if self._rightchild and distance + max_dist >= self._median:
            yield self._rightchild

        # If the function arrives here, the generator will be considered empty
        # There are no more than two values: the left and the right children

*Caller:*

    # Create an empty list and a list with the current object reference
    result, candidates = list(), [self]

    # Loop on candidates (they contain only one element at the beginning)
    while candidates:

        # Get the last candidate and remove it from the list
        node = candidates.pop()

        # Get the distance between obj and the candidate
        distance = node._get_dist(obj)

        # If the distance is ok, then you can fill in the result
        if distance <= max_dist and distance >= min_dist:
            result.extend(node._values)

        # Add the children of the candidate to the candidate's list
        # so the loop will keep running until it has looked
        # at all the children of the children of the children, etc. of the candidate
        candidates.extend(node._get_child_candidates(distance, min_dist, max_dist))

    return result

This code contains several smart parts:

- The loop iterates on a list, but the list expands while the loop is being iterated. It's a concise way to go through all these nested data even if it's a bit dangerous since you can end up with an infinite loop. In this case, `candidates.extend(node._get_child_candidates(distance, min_dist, max_dist))` exhausts all the values of the generator, but `while` keeps creating new generator objects which will produce different values from the previous ones since it's not applied on the same node.

- The `extend()` method is a list object method that expects an iterable and adds its values to the list.

Usually, we pass a list to it:

    >>> a = [1, 2]
    >>> b = [3, 4]
    >>> a.extend(b)
    >>> print(a)
    [1, 2, 3, 4]

But in your code, it gets a generator, which is good because:

1. You don't need to read the values twice.
2. You may have a lot of children and you don't want them all stored in memory.

And it works because Python does not care if the argument of a method is a list or not. Python expects iterables so it will work with strings, lists, tuples, and generators! This is called duck typing and is one of the reasons why Python is so cool. But this is another story, for another question...

You can stop here, or read a little bit to see an advanced use of a generator:

Controlling a generator exhaustion
------

    >>> class Bank(): # Let's create a bank, building ATMs
    ...    crisis = False
    ...    def create_atm(self):
    ...        while not self.crisis:
    ...            yield "$100"
    >>> hsbc = Bank() # When everything's ok the ATM gives you as much as you want
    >>> corner_street_atm = hsbc.create_atm()
    >>> print(corner_street_atm.next())
    $100
    >>> print(corner_street_atm.next())
    $100
    >>> print([corner_street_atm.next() for cash in range(5)])
    ['$100', '$100', '$100', '$100', '$100']
    >>> hsbc.crisis = True # Crisis is coming, no more money!
    >>> print(corner_street_atm.next())
    <type 'exceptions.StopIteration'>
    >>> wall_street_atm = hsbc.create_atm() # It's even true for new ATMs
    >>> print(wall_street_atm.next())
    <type 'exceptions.StopIteration'>
    >>> hsbc.crisis = False # The trouble is, even post-crisis the ATM remains empty
    >>> print(corner_street_atm.next())
    <type 'exceptions.StopIteration'>
    >>> brand_new_atm = hsbc.create_atm() # Build a new one to get back in business
    >>> for cash in brand_new_atm:
    ...    print cash
    $100
    $100
    $100
    $100
    $100
    $100
    $100
    $100
    $100
    ...

It can be useful for various things like controlling access to a resource.

Itertools, your best friend
-----

The `itertools` module contains special functions to manipulate iterables. Ever wish to duplicate a generator?
Chain two generators? Group values in a nested list with a one-liner? `Map / Zip` without creating another list?

Then just `import itertools`.

An example? Let's see the possible orders of arrival for a four-horse race:

    >>> horses = [1, 2, 3, 4]
    >>> races = itertools.permutations(horses)
    >>> print(races)
    <itertools.permutations object at 0xb754f1dc>
    >>> print(list(itertools.permutations(horses)))
    [(1, 2, 3, 4),
     (1, 2, 4, 3),
     (1, 3, 2, 4),
     (1, 3, 4, 2),
     (1, 4, 2, 3),
     (1, 4, 3, 2),
     (2, 1, 3, 4),
     (2, 1, 4, 3),
     (2, 3, 1, 4),
     (2, 3, 4, 1),
     (2, 4, 1, 3),
     (2, 4, 3, 1),
     (3, 1, 2, 4),
     (3, 1, 4, 2),
     (3, 2, 1, 4),
     (3, 2, 4, 1),
     (3, 4, 1, 2),
     (3, 4, 2, 1),
     (4, 1, 2, 3),
     (4, 1, 3, 2),
     (4, 2, 1, 3),
     (4, 2, 3, 1),
     (4, 3, 1, 2),
     (4, 3, 2, 1)]


Understanding the inner mechanisms of iteration
------

Iteration is a process implying iterables (implementing the `__iter__()` method) and iterators (implementing the `__next__()` method).
Iterables are any objects you can get an iterator from. Iterators are objects that let you iterate on iterables.

question.body_html:
What functionality does the yield keyword in Python provide?

For example, I'm trying to understand this code1:

def _get_child_candidates(self, distance, min_dist, max_dist):
    if self._leftchild and distance - max_dist < self._median:
        yield self._leftchild
    if self._rightchild and distance + max_dist >= self._median:
        yield self._rightchild

And this is the caller:

result, candidates = [], [self]
while candidates:
    node = candidates.pop()
    distance = node._get_dist(obj)
    if distance <= max_dist and distance >= min_dist:
        result.extend(node._values)
    candidates.extend(node._get_child_candidates(distance, min_dist, max_dist))
return result

What happens when the method _get_child_candidates is called? Is a list returned? A single element? Is it called again? When will subsequent calls stop?

1. This piece of code was written by Jochen Schulz (jrschulz), who made a great Python library for metric spaces. This is the link to the complete source: Module mspace.

post.description:
Questions on one Stack Exchange site matching free text (`q`: one term or up to 5 searched together), tags, or title/body text, optionally inside a creation-date window (`fromdate`/`todate`) and score/date bounds (`min`/`max`); `accepted: true` keeps only questions with an accepted answer. Returns question records (bodies only with `include_body: true`) plus per-term counts, total, has_more and quota; `question_id` and `accepted_answer_id` feed `question` and `answer`.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

accepted.description: true: only questions with an accepted answer; false: only without.

body.description: Text that must appear in the body.

fromdate.description: Lower bound on the question's creation time, inclusive: Unix seconds, `YYYY-MM-DD` or an RFC 3339 date-time (UTC).

include_body.description: true adds body_html/body_markdown to every question; off by default because bodies dominate the response size.

key.description: Optional Stack Exchange application key. Raises the per-IP quota from 300 to 10,000 requests per day. Keys are public identifiers, not secrets.

max.description: Upper bound on the sort field: score for `sort: votes`, Unix seconds for `activity` or `creation`. Not accepted with `relevance`.

min.description: Lower bound on the sort field: score for `sort: votes`, Unix seconds for `activity` or `creation`. Not accepted with `relevance`.

nottagged.description: None of these tags may be present.

page.description: page

q.description: Free-text query matched against title and body, or up to 5 such terms searched in one call (one upstream request per term; `questions` is the merged, de-duplicated union and `terms` reports each term's own count and total). The site's search syntax applies: `[tag]` matches a tag, quotes match an exact phrase.

site.description: Stack Exchange site API parameter, e.g. stackoverflow, superuser, math, askubuntu, english, physics. Use `sites` to list them. Pattern: ^[a-z0-9]+(\.[a-z0-9]+)*$.

sort.description: Defaults to `relevance`, or to `creation` when `fromdate` or `todate` is given so a date window reads as a timeline.

tagged.description: Every tag must be present on the question.

title.description: Text that must appear in the title.

todate.description: Upper bound on the question's creation time, inclusive: Unix seconds, `YYYY-MM-DD` or an RFC 3339 date-time (UTC). A date-only value covers that whole day.

url.description: A pasted site search URL (https://stackoverflow.com/search?q=..., any Stack Exchange host) or tag listing URL (https://superuser.com/questions/tagged/windows+powershell). The site comes from the host, `q` from the search URL and `tagged` from the listing path; `tab` maps to `sort` (a tag listing defaults to `creation`, like the site). Not combinable with `q` or `tagged`; an explicit `site` must match the host.

post.description:
Season-long rankings for drafts or trades.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

limit.description: Return only the first N players. Omit for the whole list.

position.description: Position. FLX is RB/WR/TE, ALL is every position.

scoring.description: Scoring format: standard, half-point PPR or full PPR. Default PPR.

default.description: Error response; upstream passthrough responses may use provider formats

x-aisa-response-pending.reason: public success response has no authoritative payload declaration

response.text:
The total value of investment in building construction edged up $25.1 million (+0.1%) to $23.5 billion in August. An increase in the non-residential sector (+1.0%) was moderated by a slight decline in the residential sector (-0.3%). Year over year, investment in building construction grew 7.9% in August.

On a constant dollar basis (2023=100), the total value of investment in building construction edged down 0.1% from the previous month to $21.2 billion in August, but it was up 4.7% year over year.

## Institutional and commercial components drive growth in non-residential investment

In August, the value of investment in non-residential building construction increased $70.5 million to $7.4 billion. Both the institutional (+1.9%) and commercial (+0.8%) components contributed to the increase, while the industrial component (-0.1%) showed little change.

Investment in institutional construction rose $43.5 million to $2.4 billion in August. Gains in Ontario (+$35.9 million) and Quebec (+$15.3 million) were moderated by declines in British Columbia (-$4.6 million) and Alberta (-$3.1 million). Investment in schools and education building construction led to the increase in the institutional component, driven by major projects in the Toronto and Montréal census metropolitan areas.

Investment in commercial construction grew $27.9 million to $3.6 billion in August. Ontario (+$18.5 million) and Quebec (+$8.0 million) were the primary contributors to the increase.

Meanwhile, investment in industrial construction edged down $0.8 million to $1.5 billion in August. This modest change was largely attributable to Quebec (-$6.6 million), Alberta (-$3.8 million) and Ontario (-$3.0 million). The gain in British Columbia (+$12.5 million) partially offset the overall decline.

## Investment in residential construction edges down

In August, investment in residential building construction edged down $45.4 million to $16.1 billion. The single-family component (-1.3%) led the slight decline, while the multi-unit component increased 0.6%.

Investment in single-family home construction was down $98.3 million to $7.6 billion in August. British Columbia (-$46.5 million) and Quebec (-$45.7 million) drove the decrease and were supported by declines across four other provinces and two territories.

Meanwhile, investment in multi-unit construction rose $52.9 million to $8.5 billion in August. Gains in Quebec (+$74.7 million) and British Columbia (+$65.2 million) were partially offset by declines in five provinces and one territory, led by Ontario (-$79.4 million).

For more information on construction, please visit the Construction statistics portal.

For more information on housing, please visit the Housing statistics portal.

## Note to readers

This content was created with the assistance of a generative artificial intelligence (AI) tool and refined and verified by Statistics Canada experts. To learn more about how the agency uses AI responsibly, please visit the Trust Centre.

Table 34-10-0286 has been archived on the Statistics Canada website and will no longer be updated but may still be viewed. The successor table is 34-10-0293, and the information from January 2017 onwards that was in table 34-10-0286 is still available in the new table, except for the constant dollar series, which has been rebased to 2023=100. Constant dollar data for January and February 2017 represent an average between the old base year (2012=100) and the new base year (2023=100) and should be used with caution. The 2017 data series will be backcasted and the figures will be revised with the release of our annual revision.

Data are subject to revisions based on late responses, delayed construction start dates for large projects, methodological changes, classification updates, price index updates for constant dollar series, benchmarking and adjustments to ad hoc macroeconomic events. Unadjusted data have been revised back to 2021. Seasonally adjusted data have been revised back to 2018.

Data presented in this release are seasonally adjusted with current dollar values unless otherwise stated. Using seasonally adjusted data allows month-to-month and quarter-to-quarter comparisons by removing the effects of seasonal variations. For information on seasonal adjustment, see the page Seasonal adjustment: Concepts and interpretation, 2026.

Monthly estimates for constant dollars are calculated using quarterly deflators from the Building Construction Price Index (18-10-0289-01). The monthly indexes used for the deflation process were part of a methodology review to increase the quality of the constant dollar and seasonally adjusted series. The indexes previously displayed a step pattern because of less frequent collection.

Detailed data on investment activity by type of building and type of work are now available in the unadjusted current dollar series.

The trade and services subcomponent includes buildings such as retail and wholesale outlets, retail complexes and motor vehicle show rooms. More detailed information can be found on the Integrated Metadatabase at Types of Building Structure - 2.2.1 - Trade and services.

## Next release

Data on investment in building construction for September will be released on November 19.

## Contact information

For more information, or to enquire about the concepts, methods or data quality of this release, contact us (toll-free 1-800-263-1136; 514-283-8300; infostats@statcan.gc.ca) or Media Relations (statcan.mediahotline-ligneinfomedias.statcan@statcan.gc.ca).

Cards To Chase: Autographs or memorabilia cards of Babe Ruth, Lou Gehrig, Mickey Mantle, Ted Williams, Roberto Clemente, Satchel Paige, Jimmie Foxx, and others across sets like The Spectacular Card Autograph and Memorabilia Booklet cards, Signature Tag Teams cards, Museum Cuts Booklet cards, Spectacular Spikes cards, Spirit of '76 Signatures and Memorbailia cards, and additional hits, inserts, variations, and parallels.
response.description_html:
After a grand slam debut in 2025, Leaf Spectacular Baseball is back for 2026 and taking the product to another level!

Look for an impressive lineup of legendary game-used memorabilia celebrating baseball's rich history. Spectacular Spikes makes its debut with large pieces from the bottom of game-used baseball cleats. These distinctive memorabilia cards bring collectors one step closer to pieces of baseball history. In honor of America's birthday, look for Spirit of '76 Signatures and Memorabilia featuring baseball stars and memorabilia connected to the historic 1976 season. This patriotic addition brings stars and stripes to the 2026 Spectacular Baseball lineup.

New for 2026, Signature Tag Team combines autographs with tags from game-used jerseys for a dynamic memorabilia experience. Collectors can also look for exciting multi-sign memorabilia cards featuring some of baseball's biggest names. Another exciting addition for 2026 is Spectacular Card booklet cards. Just as the name suggests, these booklets are designed to be Spectacular! Look for astonishing beautiful booklet cards featuring either 12 memorabilia pieces or 12 signatures! Also new for 2026, look for Museum Cuts Booklet cards.

Look for two or three multi-sign cards and at least one booklet card in every case! Find memorabilia cards throughout the product from baseball legends like Babe Ruth, Lou Gehrig, Mickey Mantle, Ted Williams, Roberto Clemente, Satchel Paige, Jimmie Foxx, and many more!

products.description:
The Jordan 4 Retro London gives the AJ4 a look shaped by the city in its name. Dark Smoke Grey suede and textured overlays create a worn, concrete inspired appearance, with Hemp and Red Bark bringing earthy contrast. The darker palette keeps the shoe restrained from a distance, but its materials and small details make it rewarding to examine up close.

London references appear throughout the release. Nike LDN branding marks the heel tab and hangtag, while an upside down "SAY LESS" tag sits beneath the tongue. Red Bark laces are also included, giving collectors another way to wear the pair while keeping its original accessories together. The release was presented as a UK and European exclusive, making its regional identity central to the design rather than simply a nickname.

For AJ4 collectors, this pair offers a specific city story through color, texture, and branding. Those details give it a distinct place beside more widely released Jordan 4s. The Jordan 4 Retro London released September 12, 2026, with a retail price of $230.
products.title: Jordan 4 Retro London

products.description:
The Air Jordan 9 Retro OG Space Jam 2026 revives one of the most beloved and culturally significant colorways in Jordan Brand history, combining white, true red, and black to honor the original silhouette's connection to the beloved Space Jam film. Michael Jordan's Space Jam appearance remains one of the most iconic crossovers between basketball and Hollywood entertainment, giving this colorway genuine cinematic and cultural significance beyond a standard sneaker release. The OG designation reflects a faithful return to the exact color story and construction associated with this legendary release.

Space Jam holds a special place within both basketball and film history, representing a genuinely unique crossover moment that introduced Michael Jordan's legacy to audiences well beyond traditional basketball fandom. This white, true red, and black combination has become deeply embedded within Jordan Brand's storytelling, consistently ranking among the most celebrated and nostalgic color stories the Jordan 9 has ever produced. Collectors who appreciate both basketball history and this iconic film crossover find this Space Jam release a genuinely significant way to own a piece of this legendary cultural moment.

The Air Jordan 9 Retro OG Space Jam 2026 was released on September 19, 2026 with a retail price of $215.
products.title: Jordan 9 Retro OG Space Jam (2026)

products.description:
The Jordan 4 Retro J Balvin Lemonade covers the AJ4 in shades of yellow that make the collaboration recognizable at a glance. Croc textured leather adds depth across the upper, so the color does more than carry the design on its own. J Balvin’s upside down smiley face appears on one heel, while Nike Air branding marks the other, continuing the uneven branding details found in his Jordan releases.

Smaller touches connect the pair to Balvin’s Colombian roots. The lace dubraes carry "JUST DO IT." and "SOLO HAZLO.", and the color story draws on the vivid scenery associated with Medellín and Colombia’s Caño Cristales river. For collectors who have followed his previous Air Jordans, this marks his move to the Jordan 4 after collaborations on earlier models. Its bright treatment gives the partnership a new look while preserving the AJ4’s familiar structure.

It is a bold pair for Balvin fans and AJ4 collectors who enjoy color and close up details. The Jordan 4 Retro J Balvin Lemonade releases September 25, 2026, with a retail price of $225.
products.title: Jordan 4 Retro J Balvin Lemonade

products.description:
The Air Jordan 4 Retro Rare Air Tour Yellow brings a vibrant, high visibility colorway into the beloved Jordan 4 silhouette, combining white, tour yellow, dark blue grey, and black into a genuinely striking presentation. The Rare Air naming ties this release to Michael Jordan's legendary competitive excellence, a phrase often associated with his singular, unmatched basketball talent. Tour yellow gives this pair significant standout presence, distinguishing it clearly from more common Jordan 4 color releases through its bold, energetic accent.

Rare Air as a concept has carried special significance within Jordan Brand's storytelling, celebrating Michael Jordan's singular basketball genius and the rarefied air of excellence he operated within throughout his career. This tour yellow execution gives the Jordan 4 genuine visual boldness, appealing to collectors who want their retro pairs to command serious attention. Fans of both Jordan Brand's storied competitive legacy and vibrant, high visibility colorways find this Rare Air release a compelling way to engage with the silhouette's continued evolution.

The Air Jordan 4 Retro Rare Air Tour Yellow was released on September 5, 2026 with a retail price of $220.
products.title: Jordan 4 Retro Rare Air Tour Yellow (2026)

products.description:
The Air Jordan 4 Retro Toro Bravo (2026) brings back one of the most recognizable non-OG colorways in the Jordan 4 archive, first introduced in 2013 during a wave of bold, lifestyle-driven releases. Dressed in fire red with white, black, and cement grey accents, the sneaker leans into high-impact color blocking that instantly stands out. The red nubuck upper gives the silhouette depth and texture, while black wings and midsole hits ground the design with contrast.

post.description:
Recent sale prices for a product or one size. The site exposes only the most recent `first` sales; there is no older-page cursor through the public operations.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。

country.description: StockX market: US (prices in USD) or GB (prices in GBP). Other markets exist upstream but were not verified.

first.description: How many recent sales (the web app asks for 20).

id.description: Product urlKey (the slug in https://stockx.com/{urlKey}) or product UUID. Pattern: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,199}$.

variant_id.description: Size variant UUID from get_product; restricts the sales to that size. Pattern: ^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$.

default.description: Error response; upstream passthrough responses may use provider formats

response.body_html:
Thanks to everyone who commented last week with prediction markets I missed. Two of them seemed to be especially interesting.

Polymarket is another cryptocurrency-based prediction market. It's got about two dozen contracts open, and some of them are pretty big - $5 million plus! With that kind of money, we ought to be seeing some really good predicting! We're...not. Either there's a 6% chance that Donald Trump will be president again by March 31, or something's gone wrong.

Probably it's the second one. I tried to bet against Trump, but getting money into the market was pretty hard. You need USDCoins, a stablecoin related to Ethereum. Polymarket tries to let you buy them directly, but their app wanted me to give them a security code which never showed up, so I gave up on this. Instead I bought some USDC at Coinbase and tried to send them over. But along with the usual Ethereum gas fees, they have something called a relayer, which is supposed to collect my money and put it in my account. And it's apparently heavily backed up, and after two days my money is nowhere to be seen (though I believe them when they say that they're trying their hardest and it will probably percolate through the Ethereum network someday). Maybe everyone's having these kinds of issues and this is why the Trump contract hasn't adjusted? I'm not sure. I will keep you updated if my money ever materializes.

Kalshi is "the first regulated futures exchange dedicated to trading on event outcomes". As far as I can tell they actually did it. They got the government to agree to let them run a prediction market, regulated as investing rather than gambling. There will be a $25,000 max on contracts, so it might not be enough for the real whales, but that's still thirty times higher than existing prediction markets and enough to probably be a sea change. I talked to a representative who said they'll be "focused on creating markets in a few key categories such as climate, economics, geopolitics, energy, education, government, space, COVID, and technology", but that they remain open to potentially expanding to all sorts of other areas (except onions, which apparently have a very specific carve-out as something which it is illegal to have futures markets about, somebody please write a cyberpunk novel revolving around this). So far they're still setting things up, but they describe themselves as "ramping quickly towards launch". I am super psyched about this and will keep you all updated.

Getting back to Metaculus, let’s look at what they’ve got on AI:

Die besondere Stärke des Fraunhofer-Instituts für Elektronische Nanosysteme ENAS liegt in der Entwicklung von Smart Systems - sogenannten intelligenten Systemen für verschiedenartige Anwendungen. Die Systeme verbinden Elektronikkomponenten, Mikro- und Nanosensoren und -aktoren mit Schnittstellen zur Kommunikation. Fraunhofer ENAS entwickelt Einzelkomponenten, die Technologien für deren Fertigung aber auch Systemkonzepte und Systemintegrationstechnologien und überführt sie in die praktische Nutzung. Fraunhofer ENAS begleitet Kundenprojekte von der Idee über den Entwurf, die Technologieentwicklung oder Umsetzung anhand bestehender Technologien bis hin zum getesteten Prototyp.

 

Hier sorgen Sie für Veränderung

Für Ihre Initiativbewerbung teilen Sie uns bitte mit:

  • in welches Fachgebiet / welchen Themenbereich der Verwaltung Sie sich einbringen möchten
  • welche Erfahrungen Sie mitbringen
  • ab wann Sie zur Verfügung stehen können
  • Ihre Gehaltsvorstellung


Wir bitten um Übersendung vollständiger Bewerbungsunterlagen (Anschreiben, Lebenslauf, Zeugnisse).

 

Hiermit bringen Sie sich ein

  • Sie haben eine eigenverantwortliche und sorgfältige Arbeitsweise, sind zuverlässig und haben ein hohes Maß an Lernbereitschaft.
  • Sie verfügen über Organisationstalent, Kreativität und Hands-On-Mentalität.
  • Auch Sozialkompetenz, Team- und Kommunikationsfähigkeit und Belastbarkeit zeichnen Sie aus.
  • Gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift sowie Englischkenntnisse runden Ihr Profil ab.

 

Was wir für Sie bereithalten

  • ein spannendes und interdisziplinäres Arbeitsumfeld mit Verantwortung und Raum für Ihre Ideen
  • ein offenes, motiviertes Team, flache Hierarchien sowie modernste technische Ausstattung
  • eine von Kollegialität geprägte Unternehmenskultur
  • ein attraktives Gehaltspaket mit Jahressonderzahlung nach TVöD Bund, 30 Urlaubstagen, Jobticket und betrieblicher Altersvorsorge (VBL)
  • vielfältige Weiterbildungs- und Qualifizierungsmöglichkeiten 
  • optimale Work-Life-Balance durch flexible Arbeitszeiten sowie unterschiedliche Unterstützungsangebote (z.B. mobiles Arbeiten) zur Vereinbarkeit von Privatleben und Beruf

 

Wir wertschätzen und fördern die Vielfalt der Kompetenzen unserer Mitarbeitenden und begrüßen daher alle Bewerbungen – unabhängig von Alter, Geschlecht, Nationalität, ethnischer und sozialer Herkunft, Religion, Weltanschauung, Behinderung sowie sexueller Orientierung und Identität. Schwerbehinderte Menschen werden bei gleicher Eignung bevorzugt eingestellt. Unsere Aufgaben sind vielfältig und anpassbar – für Bewerber*innen mit Behinderung finden wir gemeinsam Lösungen, die ihre Fähigkeiten optimal fördern. 

Die wöchentliche Arbeitszeit beträgt 39 Stunden. Die Stelle kann auch in Teilzeit besetzt werden. Anstellung, Vergütung und Sozialleistungen basieren auf dem Tarifvertrag für den öffentlichen Dienst (TVöD). Zusätzlich kann Fraunhofer leistungs- und erfolgsabhängige variable Vergütungsbestandteile gewähren.

Mit ihrer Fokussierung auf zukunftsrelevante Schlüsseltechnologien sowie auf die Verwertung der Ergebnisse in Wirtschaft und Industrie spielt die Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft eine zentrale Rolle im Innovationsprozess. Als Wegweiser und Impulsgeber für innovative Entwicklungen und wissenschaftliche Exzellenz wirkt sie mit an der Gestaltung unserer Gesellschaft und unserer Zukunft.

Die besondere Stärke des Fraunhofer-Instituts für Elektronische Nanosysteme ENAS liegt in der Entwicklung von Smart Systems - sogenannten intelligenten Systemen für verschiedenartige Anwendungen. Die Systeme verbinden Elektronikkomponenten, Mikro- und Nanosensoren und -aktoren mit Schnittstellen zur Kommunikation. Fraunhofer ENAS entwickelt Einzelkomponenten, die Technologien für deren Fertigung aber auch Systemkonzepte und Systemintegrationstechnologien und überführt sie in die praktische Nutzung. Fraunhofer ENAS begleitet Kundenprojekte von der Idee über den Entwurf, die Technologieentwicklung oder Umsetzung anhand bestehender Technologien bis hin zum getesteten Prototyp.

 

Hier sorgen Sie für Veränderung

Für Ihre Initiativbewerbung teilen Sie uns bitte mit:

  • in welches Fachgebiet / welchen Themenbereich der Verwaltung Sie sich einbringen möchten
  • welche Erfahrungen Sie mitbringen
  • ab wann Sie zur Verfügung stehen können
  • Ihre Gehaltsvorstellung


Wir bitten um Übersendung vollständiger Bewerbungsunterlagen (Anschreiben, Lebenslauf, Zeugnisse).

 

Hiermit bringen Sie sich ein

  • Sie haben eine eigenverantwortliche und sorgfältige Arbeitsweise, sind zuverlässig und haben ein hohes Maß an Lernbereitschaft.
  • Sie verfügen über Organisationstalent, Kreativität und Hands-On-Mentalität.
  • Auch Sozialkompetenz, Team- und Kommunikationsfähigkeit und Belastbarkeit zeichnen Sie aus.
  • Gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift sowie Englischkenntnisse runden Ihr Profil ab.

 

Was wir für Sie bereithalten

  • ein spannendes und interdisziplinäres Arbeitsumfeld mit Verantwortung und Raum für Ihre Ideen
  • ein offenes, motiviertes Team, flache Hierarchien sowie modernste technische Ausstattung
  • eine von Kollegialität geprägte Unternehmenskultur
  • ein attraktives Gehaltspaket mit Jahressonderzahlung nach TVöD Bund, 30 Urlaubstagen, Jobticket und betrieblicher Altersvorsorge (VBL)
  • vielfältige Weiterbildungs- und Qualifizierungsmöglichkeiten 
  • optimale Work-Life-Balance durch flexible Arbeitszeiten sowie unterschiedliche Unterstützungsangebote (z.B. mobiles Arbeiten) zur Vereinbarkeit von Privatleben und Beruf

 

Wir wertschätzen und fördern die Vielfalt der Kompetenzen unserer Mitarbeitenden und begrüßen daher alle Bewerbungen – unabhängig von Alter, Geschlecht, Nationalität, ethnischer und sozialer Herkunft, Religion, Weltanschauung, Behinderung sowie sexueller Orientierung und Identität. Schwerbehinderte Menschen werden bei gleicher Eignung bevorzugt eingestellt. Unsere Aufgaben sind vielfältig und anpassbar – für Bewerber*innen mit Behinderung finden wir gemeinsam Lösungen, die ihre Fähigkeiten optimal fördern. 

Die wöchentliche Arbeitszeit beträgt 39 Stunden. Die Stelle kann auch in Teilzeit besetzt werden. Anstellung, Vergütung und Sozialleistungen basieren auf dem Tarifvertrag für den öffentlichen Dienst (TVöD). Zusätzlich kann Fraunhofer leistungs- und erfolgsabhängige variable Vergütungsbestandteile gewähren.

Mit ihrer Fokussierung auf zukunftsrelevante Schlüsseltechnologien sowie auf die Verwertung der Ergebnisse in Wirtschaft und Industrie spielt die Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft eine zentrale Rolle im Innovationsprozess. Als Wegweiser und Impulsgeber für innovative Entwicklungen und wissenschaftliche Exzellenz wirkt sie mit an der Gestaltung unserer Gesellschaft und unserer Zukunft. 

Bereit für Veränderung? Dann bewerben Sie sich jetzt, und machen Sie einen Unterschied! Nach Eingang Ihrer Online-Bewerbung erhalten Sie eine automatische Empfangsbestätigung. Dann melden wir uns schnellstmöglich und sagen Ihnen, wie es weitergeht. 
 

 

 

 

 

Fragen zur Stelle richten Sie bitte an:

www.enas.fraunhofer.de

post.description:
Start here with any career-site URL running on SAP SuccessFactors / jobs2web (rmkcdn.successfactors.com assets, /job/{slug}/{id}/ posting URLs). Read `facets` for filterable fields, page with next_offset, then call get_job with a row's url (or career_site + job_id) for the full description.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

career_site.description: Any URL of an employer's SuccessFactors career site (custom domain such as https://jobs.fraunhofer.de/, https://careers.ey.com/ or https://basf.jobs/; a bare domain, a /search/ results URL with q, locationsearch and optionsFacetsDD_* parameters, or a posting URL are fine).

filters.description: Facet filters, ANDed: each {field, value} uses a `field` from a previous search_jobs `facets`. Values are what the site stores, not the label shown: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes for country (DE), language codes for lang (en, de), and the displayed text for other fields (exact match; a value the site doesn't know returns no results). When omitted, optionsFacetsDD_* parameters of a pasted search URL apply. Not available on sitemap-backed sites.

locale.description: Site language as the platform names it, e.g. de_DE or en_US; defaults to the site's default. Pattern: ^[a-z]{2,3}_[A-Z]{2}$.

location.description: Free-text location search (the site's locationsearch), e.g. Berlin. When omitted a pasted URL's locationsearch applies.

offset.description: Result offset (the site's startrow): 0 for the first page, then the previous page's next_offset.

query.description: Keyword search (the site's q). Omit to list everything; when omitted a pasted URL's q applies.

response.attribution: Source: the named employer's SAP SuccessFactors career site

<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

spec.description: Spec slug of that class, to keep only builds or orders that lead in that tree: druid balance/feral/restoration, hunter beast-mastery/marksmanship/survival, mage arcane/fire/frost, paladin holy/protection/retribution, priest discipline/holy/shadow, rogue assassination/combat/subtlety, shaman elemental/enhancement/restoration, warlock affliction/demonology/destruction, warrior arms/fury/protection.

response.attribution: Counts from Talents Forever (https://talentsforever.com/), the site's own tally of builds planned on it. A count of what people plan, not a tier list.

brackets.holders: 1,722 of the 16,848 Arms builds that reach level 19 hold these points, 10.2%.
brackets.note: Across all 16,848 of those builds the talents taken most in these levels are Improved Rend (83%), Improved Tactical Mastery (65%), Deflection (49%) and Improved Heroic Strike (46%).

brackets.holders: 537 of the 4,294 Arms builds that reach level 29 hold these points, 12.5%.
brackets.note: Across all 4,294 of those builds the talents taken most in these levels are Deep Wounds (94%), Improved Overpower (81%), Anger Management (78%) and Impale (73%).

Fewer than 25 of the builds that follow the order above reach these levels the same way, so the order stops here rather than guess. Of the 1,015 that reach them, most put points in Sweeping Strikes (86%), Weaponmaster (79%), Two-Handed Weapon Specialization (76%) and Bloodthrill (67%).

orders.summary: The order runs to level 29: Improved Rend ×3, Deflection ×2, Improved Tactical Mastery ×5, Improved Overpower ×2, Deep Wounds ×3, Anger Management, Impale ×2, Two-Handed Weapon Specialization ×2.

post.description:
Use for review text and ratings of a known Target product (url or tcin from featured or variants). To sync incrementally, call with sort=newest and since set to the latest submitted_at you already hold, or stop paging at a known review_id. A query exposes at most 2550 reviews; larger products are read per star rating, and the output warns where a rating bucket is cut short.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous call. Pass every other input unchanged.

page_size.description: Reviews per source page; a call reads up to 8 pages.

rating.description: Only reviews with this star rating.

since.description: With sort=newest: stop at the first review submitted before this UTC date or datetime (YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). Use it for incremental sync.

sort.description: newest is by submission date, descending. Within one rating or one query, ties keep newest first.

tcin.description: Numeric TCIN, as returned by featured and variants. Use instead of url. Pattern: ^[0-9]{6,12}$.

url.description: HTTPS www.target.com product URL ending /-/A-<numeric TCIN>, without query or fragment. Pattern: ^https://www\.target\.com/p/(?:[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+/)?-/A-[0-9]{6,12}$.

To find tenders by keyword/filters or to resolve a 12-digit reference number to its tender_id_string before calling get_tender.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->

<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

activity_id.description: Main activity id from list_lookups kind=activities.

agency_code.description: 12-digit agency code from list_lookups kind=agencies. Pattern: ^[0-9]{12}$.

booklet_price_range.description: ConditionaBookletRange band 0-6 as offered by the site's price filter.

category.description: TenderCategory: 0 all, 2 active/open, 3 enquiries stage, 4 offers stage, 5 opening stage, 6 awarded, 8 finished. Omitted = the site's default (all).

page.description: 1-based page number. The response reports the total and the runner's `next_cursor` carries the next page number.

page_size.description: Rows per page, 1-24 (the server caps every page at 24 rows).

published_within.description: PublishDateId: 1 any time (default here), 2 last two days, 3 last week, 4 last month, 5 last three months (the site's own UI default).

query.description: Free-text keyword (MultipleSearch): matched against tender name, number, agency.

sort.description: Sort key.

tender_type_id.description: Tender type id from list_lookups kind=tender_types (1 = منافسة عامة / public tender).

post.description:
Pass `guid` or `url` from an atm_search row, or an `atm_id` such as `NS1333` (resolved through the list's id filter, so only open ATMs resolve by id; closed ones need their GUID). Closed notices redirect to /Atm/ShowClosed/{guid} and come back with `status: closed`. Briefing requirements are free text in the instructions/conditions fields; `briefing_mentioned` and `briefing_excerpts` flag them, they do not structure them. An unknown id or GUID is not_found.

url.description: A pasted https://www.tenders.gov.au/Atm/Show/{guid}, /Atm/ShowClosed/{guid}, /Atm/Show?Id={guid} or /Advert/Show/{guid} URL.

response.conditions_for_participation:

Certificate for working at heights
response.description:
Questacon requires a permanent adjustable lighting and projection rig for Gallery 8, the Drum. The purpose of the rig is to expand lighting capability for a wide variety of future exhibition installations in the space. This will include improved lighting for items anywhere on the on the gallery floor as well as suspended in the large void above. The rig will enable the creation of dynamic lighting, projection, and visual effects particularly overhead in the tall gallery void. Together with existing hanging points, the rig will provide the ability to suspend large objects in the void ranging from sculptural artwork pieces to fabrics, scrims or string curtains for large scale projection effects.
Questacon has developed a rig concept that features a 12m diameter box truss ring called the Halo - see concept drawings. This truss will require new suspension points from the existing structural steel work above the Gallery 8 ceiling. The Halo will be able to be raised or lowered to adjust the display height for a particular exhibition as well as allow for installation, cleaning, and maintenance from the gallery floor. The truss is to be black to disappear into the dark void and the suspension cables should be visually minimal. Winches, motors and other equipment will be hidden above the gallery ceiling while a control interface should be provided in an accessible location from the gallery floor whilst not adding any visual clutter to the exhibition space. The truss will need power for lighting and projection equipment, lighting and projection protocols, as well as data. A reticulation system above the gallery ceiling is required for minimal and discrete power and data cable management.
An 8.5 metre diameter black circular box truss, is also envisioned for the space, suspended from existing cleats or pulley cleats. This will provide multiple customisable rigging points for objects suspended in the space, sail tracking around the perimeter to hang scrims or string curtains, and can also carry lighting and projectors on droppers or risers. This truss will be raised and lowered independently of the Halo, and will need its own power and data cable system, as well as a control system. Again, equipment is to be hidden above the ceiling to minimise visual impact.
response.other_instructions: All personal on site must hold a valid Working with Vulnerable People card or state equivalent.
response.title: Gallery 8 Lighting Halo

post.description:
Use for 'what was published/started/ends between X and Y'. The API pages 100 releases at a time behind an opaque cursor; `limit` trims a page and the continuation cursor resumes exactly where the previous call stopped. Dates must be full UTC timestamps `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. An empty window is a normal empty result; a reversed or malformed window is invalid_input.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->

<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

cursor.description: Opaque continuation from a previous call's `next_cursor`. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,3}@[A-Za-z0-9._=-]*$.

date_type.description: Which contract date the window applies to (the API's DateType path segment).

limit.description: Maximum contract records to return in this call (the API page holds up to 100 releases).

post.description:
To find tenders by keyword (e.g. cleaning), agency, region, state or date range. Ids for public_authority_id, issuing_business_id, region_id and pre_qualification_level_id come from lookups.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->

<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

aboriginal_participation.description: Aboriginal Procurement Policy participation filter (form field app).

dcsp.description: Delivering Community Services in Partnership policy filter.

issuing_business_id.description: Issuing agency id from lookups(issuing_agencies); -1 or omitted = any.

keywords.description: Keyword(s), max 50 characters as the form allows. Matched over request number, title and description.

match.description: exact: the keywords as one phrase (form value exactMatch); any: any of the words (anyWord).

pre_qualification_level_id.description: Builder pre-qualification level id from lookups(pre_qualification_levels); -1 or omitted = any.

public_authority_id.description: Public authority id from lookups(public_authorities); -1 or omitted = any.

region_id.description: Region id from lookups(regions), e.g. 7 = Perth Metropolitan; -1 or omitted = any.

state.description: Request state, using the form's own values (Open = Current, Early Advice = Future, NoOffsReceived = No Offers Received, AllOffsDeclined = All Offers Declined).

unspsc_codes.description: Up to three UNSPSC codes (form fields unspscCode1..3).

response.biography:
Florence Pugh (born 3 January 1996) is an English actress. Her accolades include a British Independent Film Award, in addition to nominations for an Academy Award and three BAFTA Awards.

After making her acting debut in the drama film The Falling (2014), Pugh gained praise for starring in the independent drama Lady Macbeth (2016) and the miniseries The Little Drummer Girl (2018). Her international breakthrough came in 2019 with her portrayals of professional wrestler Paige in the sports film Fighting with My Family, a despondent American woman in the horror film Midsommar, and Amy March in the period drama Little Women. For the last of these, she was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress.

Pugh has played Yelena Belova in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, starring in the films Black Widow (2021), Thunderbolts* (2025), and Spider-Man: Brand New Day (2026), as well as the Disney+ miniseries Hawkeye (2021). In her highest-grossing releases, she voiced Goldilocks in Puss in Boots: The Last Wish (2022), and portrayed Jean Tatlock in Oppenheimer (2023) and Princess Irulan in Dune: Part Two (2024); she also continued to gain praise for her performances in dramas such as We Live in Time (2024).

Description above from the Wikipedia article Florence Pugh, licensed under CC-BY-SA, full list of contributors on Wikipedia.

Her accolades include a British Independent Film Award, in addition to nominations for an Academy Award and three BAFTA Awards.\n\nAfter making her acting debut in the drama film The Falling (2014), Pugh gained praise for starring in the independent drama Lady Macbeth (2016) and the miniseries The Little Drummer Girl (2018). Her international breakthrough came in 2019 with her portrayals of professional wrestler Paige in the sports film Fighting with My Family, a despondent American woman in the horror film Midsommar, and Amy March in the period drama Little Women. For the last of these, she was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress.\n\nPugh has played Yelena Belova in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, starring in the films Black Widow (2021), Thunderbolts* (2025), and Spider-Man: Brand New Day (2026), as well as the Disney+ miniseries Hawkeye (2021). post.description:
Catalogue, new products (sort created-descending), prices or stock of a store on Tiendanube / Nuvemshop (*.mitiendanube.com, *.lojavirtualnuvem.com.br or a custom domain). Get category paths from list_categories and product details from get_product.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

category.description: One category: its path (/ropa/remeras/) or its URL on the store, from list_categories. Omit for the all-products listing.

page.description: Page number (default 1); the page size is the store theme's.

query.description: Keywords matched (accent-insensitive, every word) against product URL slugs from the store's sitemap. Cannot be combined with category or sort.

sort.description: Storefront sort order; omit for the store's default. created-descending lists the newest products first; user is the store's featured order.

post.description:
Find shows by city, keyword or date, then pass a show id to show or showtimes.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
按用量计费；默认请求预估费用：$0.0005 USD（不是固定价格）。 声明的单位费率：每 firecrawl_credit $0.0001 USD。 最终费用以账户适用价格及实际结算为准。
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

date.description: Only shows with a performance on this local date, YYYY-MM-DD. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

location_id.description: TodayTix city id from locations (1 New York, 2 London, 3 Chicago, 4 SF Bay Area, 5 Los Angeles, 6 Washington DC, 7 Boston, 17 Sydney, 18 Melbourne, 19 Brisbane, 93 Perth, 95 Adelaide).

max_price.description: Only shows whose lowest regular price is at most this amount in the city's currency.

offset.description: 0-based offset; use next_offset from the previous page.

query.description: Keyword matched against show names (e.g. `hamilton`). Omit to browse the whole city.

sort_by.description: `price` (lowest regular price) or `recent_views` (recently viewed); omitted, the site orders by popularity.

sort_order.description: Direction for sort_by; the site's default when omitted.

timezone.description: IANA timezone the `date` is in. Defaults to the city's timezone for the known location ids; required with `date` for any other id.

shows.name: Hamilton on Broadway
shows.sales_message: Ten years on, this iconic masterpiece still has the power to blow you away. Join the revolution.

response.description:
The Stephen Sondheim Theatre is a treasured gem within the heart of New York City. Located in the bustling Times Square district, it stands proudly, retaining its historical charm midst contemporary edifices. The theatre, formerly known as Henry Miller's Theatre, is deeply rooted in theatrical history, having hosted numerous Broadway classics since its inception in 1918. It boasts art nouveau architecture bathed in gentle, welcoming lights, with intricate details that add to its grandeur. A walk inside reveals a relaxing ambiance with ornamented ceilings, beautiful chandeliers, red velvet seats, and a sizeable stage that brings performances to life. Dedicated to the legendary composer Stephen Sondheim, the theatre's rich legacy continues by staging some of the most critically acclaimed plays, musicals, and performances, all enjoyed from the comfort of its 1,055 seats. 

**How to Get There** 
Stephen Sondheim Theatre is conveniently located at 124 West 43rd Street, accessible via various modes of transportation. Visitors can reach the theatre by subway, taking the B, D, F, or M train to 42nd Street/Bryant Park or the 1, 2, 3, 7, N, Q, R, S, or W train to Times Square/42nd Street. Buses M5, M7, M20, M42, or M104 also offer routes to Times Square. For those who prefer driving, several paid parking garages are available nearby.
response.name: Stephen Sondheim Theatre
response.short_description: The Stephen Sondheim Theatre is a cherished historical venue in Times Square, known for its Broadway classics and art nouveau architecture.

response.story:
A brick, or a block: what's the difference? It seems like a negligible distinction, but we take such distinctions 
seriously-especially when it comes to Trader Joe's Cream Cheese.

Within the cheese biz, this particular presentation of Cream Cheese is known as a "brick." Brick, however, 
sounds heavy, and this creamy creation is anything but. Made for us using fresh milk and cream from cows not 
treated with rBST, it's everything you want cream cheese to be-rich, creamy, and when softened, quite spread-
able. So, rather than "brick," we'd like to refer to our Cream Cheese as a "block," as in "building block," since it 
can be a building block in so many delicious dishes.

What's that? You want examples? Sure. A simple appetizer idea: set it on a plate, top with salsa or sweet chili 
sauce and serve with tortilla chips or crackers for a Mexican or Thai inspired dip. How's that for instant versa-
tility? And speaking of dips, cream cheese is the star of any number of creamy dips. Don't forget bagels-but 
how could you forget bagels? Pretzel Bagels [sku 52370], maybe? Perhaps our favorite usage for this particular 
building block is cheesecake. If you're up to the challenge of making a cheesecake from scratch, you won't find 
a better foundation.

Perhaps the biggest WOW of all is our price of $1.69 for each eight-ounce block of certified kosher Trader Joe's 
Cream Cheese. You'll find it in our cheese case, next to other cream cheeses not in "block" form.
response.story_html:
A brick, or a block: what’s the difference? It seems like a negligible distinction, but we take such distinctions seriously—especially when it comes to Trader Joe’s Cream Cheese.

Within the cheese biz, this particular presentation of Cream Cheese is known as a “brick.” Brick, however, sounds heavy, and this creamy creation is anything but. Made for us using fresh milk and cream from cows not treated with rBST, it’s everything you want cream cheese to be—rich, creamy, and when softened, quite spread- able. So, rather than “brick,” we’d like to refer to our Cream Cheese as a “block,” as in “building block,” since it can be a building block in so many delicious dishes.

What’s that? You want examples? Sure. A simple appetizer idea: set it on a plate, top with salsa or sweet chili sauce and serve with tortilla chips or crackers for a Mexican or Thai inspired dip. How’s that for instant versa- tility? And speaking of dips, cream cheese is the star of any number of creamy dips. Don’t forget bagels—but how could you forget bagels? Perhaps our favorite usage for this particular building block is cheesecake. If you’re up to the challenge of making a cheesecake from scratch, you won’t find a better foundation.

advisories.summary:
Do not travel to North Korea due to wrongful detention and other risks.
Do not travel to North Korea due to the continuing serious risk of arrest, long-term detention, and the threat of wrongful detention of U.S. citizens.
Do not travel to the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea for any reason.
- U.S. passports cannot be used to travel to, in, or through the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK or North Korea) unless they are specially validated for such travel by the Secretary of State.
- Special validations are granted only in very limited circumstances. Review the information on how to apply for the special validation.
Because the U.S. government does not have diplomatic relations with North Korea, it cannot provide direct help to U.S. citizens in North Korea in emergencies.
- Sweden serves as the U.S. protecting power in North Korea through its Embassy in Pyongyang and provides limited consular services to U.S. citizens. Additionally, the North Korean government has often delayed or denied Swedish officials access to U.S. citizens who are detained.
- The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has issued a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) or a Special Federal Aviation Regulation (SFAR). This is due to the risks to civil aviation operating within or in the vicinity of North Korea.
- For more information U.S. citizens should consult the Federal Aviation Administration’s Prohibitions, Restrictions and Notices.
